```{r packages}
                  unit = character(), source = character())
log_number <- function(id, description, value, unit, source) {
  numbers <<- bind_rows(numbers, tibble(id = id, description = description,
                                        value = value, unit = unit, source = source))
  invisible(value)
}

# Check against the publisher: stop if a number does not match
check <- function(label, value, expected, tol = 1) {
  ok <- abs(value - expected) < tol
  cat(sprintf("%s %-72s %12s   (publisher: %s)\n", if (ok) "OK  " else "FAIL", label,
              format(round(value, 1), big.mark = ","), format(round(expected, 1), big.mark = ",")))
  if (!ok) stop(label, ": check failed")
}

fmt <- function(x, d = 0) format(round(x, d), big.mark = ",", nsmall = d)
```

# Our answer

FZS (Frankfurt Zoological Society) reports to donors and governments on
illegal gold mining around its protected areas in Peru. Today it learns
about new mining mainly from yearly satellite maps, and these maps arrive
more than a year late. Our question was: **which numbers should FZS
check every year, so it can see trouble earlier and act?**

We recommend **five indicators**. They work at three speeds:

- **Early** numbers move before new mining shows up on the maps.
- **Now** numbers show where mining is happening this quarter.
- **Late** numbers confirm, once a year, how much forest was lost. They
  are slow but trusted, so FZS can use them in donor reports.

| \# | Indicator | Speed | How often | Source |
|----|-----------|-------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Gold price in soles, after inflation, compared with its average of the last 3 years | Early | Monthly | World Bank, Central Bank of Peru (BCRP) |
| 2 | Peru's gold gap: gold exported minus gold declared as produced | Early | Monthly | BCRP |
| 3 | New mining in FZS landscapes (hectares, by quarter) | Now | Quarterly | Amazon Mining Watch, SERNANP |
| 4 | Forest turned into mining: inside reserves and buffer zones, and in all of Madre de Dios | Late | Yearly | MapBiomas Peru |
| 5 | New mining outside Madre de Dios (is mining spreading?) | Now | Quarterly | Amazon Mining Watch |

Each indicator has **one red line** (a simple rule) and **one action**
for FZS. Section 6 explains how we chose each red line and whether it
would have warned FZS in time before the 2021 to 2023 mining surge.

We also checked many other signals: gold and mercury trade, coca,
malaria in Brazil, aviation fuel, dredges in Colombia and Loreto, and
traffic on the Interoceanic Highway. They are useful **context**, but
each one has a problem that stops it from being a yearly indicator for
FZS (Section 9).

**How to read the labels.** Every claim is marked **[Description]**
(what the data show), **[Prediction]** (what may happen) or
**[Causal]** (what causes what). We make no causal claims.

# How we worked

1. **We started from FZS's problem.** The yearly maps are good but
   late. So we looked for numbers that move earlier, and for numbers
   that say *where* the mining is.
2. **We described Madre de Dios first** (Section 4). The maps give a
   *stock* (all mining land in a year). The stock rarely goes down, so
   we used *flows*: land that became mining each year, and where it came
   from.
3. **We found a trap.** Much of the big 2023 jump was water (old
   flooded pits and rivers) relabelled as mining, not new forest loss.
   So our yearly indicator counts only **forest that became mining**.
4. **We looked for early signals.** Miners respond to the gold price.
   And gold that is exported but never declared as produced shows how
   much gold comes from outside the legal system.
5. **We used quarterly satellite data** to see where mining is
   happening now, and in hectares, so the numbers can be compared with
   other sources.
6. **We checked if mining is spreading** to new places outside Madre de
   Dios.
7. **We set one red line for each indicator and tested it on the past.**
   We chose the rules after we saw the data, so the test shows what
   *would* have happened. It is not proof. The fair test is the next two
   years.
8. **We kept the other signals as context.** We say why each one is not
   a main indicator.

# Data and checks

All raw files are in `data_raw/` exactly as downloaded. Each file has one
row in `DOWNLOAD_LOG.csv`. Two Amazon Mining Watch files are too big for
the zip (113 MB and 62 MB). They are kept in `../data_large/`, next to
the replication folder, and the code below downloads them if they are
missing. Amazon Mining Watch replaces these files when its model
changes, so the checks below stop the notebook if a new download does
not match the version we used.

```{r download-large}
large <- file.path("..", "data_large")
dir.create(large, showWarnings = FALSE)
amw_file  <- file.path(large, "amazon_basin_detections.geojson")
scar_file <- file.path(large, "amazon_basin_mining_scar_masks.tif")
options(timeout = 1200)
if (!file.exists(amw_file))  download.file("https://data.source.coop/earthgenome/amazon-mining-watch/amazon_basin_detections.geojson", amw_file, mode = "wb")
if (!file.exists(scar_file)) download.file("https://data.source.coop/earthgenome/amazon-mining-watch/amazon_basin_mining_scar_masks.tif", scar_file, mode = "wb")
cat("MD5 of the detections file:", unname(tools::md5sum(amw_file)), "\n")
cat("MD5 of the scar map:       ", unname(tools::md5sum(scar_file)), "\n")
```

```{r regional-downloads}
REG <- file.path(RAW, "regional")
dir.create(REG, showWarnings = FALSE)
# Download a file only if it is missing (all files used here are already in data_raw/regional/)
get_if_missing <- function(url, file, wait = 0) {
  dest <- file.path(REG, file)
  if (!file.exists(dest)) { Sys.sleep(wait); options(timeout = 600); download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE) }
  invisible(dest)
}
ct <- "https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS?"   # UN Comtrade public preview: one year per call, no key
for (y in 2010:2025) {
  get_if_missing(paste0(ct, "reporterCode=604,170,76,68,218,862,328,740&cmdCode=7108&flowCode=X&period=", y, "&partnerCode=0"), sprintf("comtrade_gold_exports_%d.json", y), 5)

  if (y >= 2015) get_if_missing(paste0(ct, "reporterCode=604,170,76&cmdCode=842952&flowCode=M&period=", y, "&partnerCode=0"), sprintf("comtrade_excavators_%d.json", y), 5)
}

                                    sprintf("brazil_malaria_special_areas_%d.csv", y), 2)
```

## MapBiomas Peru, Collection 4

```{r mapbiomas-read}
f_pol <- file.path(RAW, "MAPBIOMAS-PERU-LULC-COL4-LIMITES-POLITICOS.xlsx")
f_za  <- file.path(RAW, "MAPBIOMAS-PERU-LULC-COL4-ZONA-AMORTIGUAMIENTO.xlsx")
f_anp <- file.path(RAW, "MAPBIOMAS-PERU-LULC-COL4-AREAS-PROTEGIDAS.xlsx")

MINING <- 30                       # class 4.2 Minería
FOREST <- c(3, 4, 5, 6)            # 1.1 Bosque, 1.2 Bosque seco, 1.3 Manglar, 1.4 Bosque inundable
WATER  <- c(26, 31, 33)            # 5. Cuerpo de agua (river, lake, aquaculture)
BEACH  <- 23                       # 4.3 Playa (river beaches)

long_years <- function(d) d %>%
  pivot_longer(matches("^y\\d{4}$"), names_to = "year", values_to = "ha") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(sub("y", "", year)))

# Coverage (stocks): one row per territory x class, one column per year
cov_pol <- read_excel(f_pol, "COVERAGE_4") %>% long_years() %>%
  transmute(biome = territory_level_2_1, department = territory_level_2_2, class, year, ha)
cov_za  <- read_excel(f_za, "COVERAGE_4") %>% long_years() %>%
  transmute(unit = territory_level_2_1, category = territory_level_3_1,
            department = territory_level_2_2, class, year, ha)
cov_anp <- read_excel(f_anp, "COVERAGE_4") %>% long_years() %>%
  transmute(unit = territory_level_2_1, category = territory_level_3_1,
            department = territory_level_2_2, class, year, ha)

# Transitions (flows): area that moved from class_from to class_to between two consecutive years
read_transitions <- function(file) {
  read_excel(file, "TRANSITION_4") %>%
    pivot_longer(matches("^p\\d{4}_\\d{4}$"), names_to = "period", values_to = "ha") %>%
    mutate(y0 = as.integer(substr(period, 2, 5)), year = as.integer(substr(period, 7, 10))) %>%
    filter(year - y0 == 1) %>%                     # keep one year periods; drop 5 year and 1985 to 2025 totals
    mutate(ha = replace_na(ha, 0))
}
tr_pol <- read_transitions(f_pol) %>% rename(unit = territory_level_2)
tr_za  <- read_transitions(f_za)  %>% rename(unit = territory_level_2)
tr_anp <- read_transitions(f_anp) %>% rename(unit = territory_level_2)
```

```{r checks-mapbiomas}
mdd_level <- cov_pol %>% filter(department == "Madre de Dios", class == MINING) %>%
  group_by(year) %>% summarise(mining_ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop")
amazon_2025 <- cov_pol %>% filter(biome == "Amazonía", class == MINING, year == 2025) %>% pull(ha) %>% sum()
tamb_za_2025 <- cov_za %>% filter(unit == "Tambopata", class == MINING, year == 2025) %>% pull(ha) %>% sum()
mdd_za_2025  <- cov_za %>% filter(department == "Madre de Dios", class == MINING, year == 2025) %>% pull(ha) %>% sum()

check("MapBiomas C4: Madre de Dios, mining, 2025 (ha)", mdd_level$mining_ha[mdd_level$year == 2025], 112622)
check("MapBiomas C4: Peru, Amazon biome, mining, 2025 (ha)", amazon_2025, 118296)
check("MapBiomas C4: Tambopata buffer zone, mining, 2025 (ha)", tamb_za_2025, 20730)
check("MapBiomas C4: all buffer zones in Madre de Dios, mining, 2025 (ha)", mdd_za_2025, 34635)

# Transitions must add up to the stock: land that stayed mining + land that came in = stock this year
tr_mdd <- tr_pol %>% filter(unit == "Madre de Dios")
recon <- tr_mdd %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(stock_from_transitions = sum(ha[class_to == MINING]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(mdd_level, by = "year")
check("Transitions reproduce the 2025 stock in Madre de Dios (ha)",
      recon$stock_from_transitions[recon$year == 2025], 112622)

log_number("chk_mdd_2025", "Mining area, Madre de Dios, 2025", mdd_level$mining_ha[mdd_level$year == 2025], "ha", "MapBiomas Peru C4, Limites politicos, COVERAGE_4, class 30")
log_number("chk_amz_2025", "Mining area, Peru Amazon biome, 2025", amazon_2025, "ha", "MapBiomas Peru C4, Limites politicos")
log_number("chk_tamb_za_2025", "Mining area, Tambopata buffer zone, 2025", tamb_za_2025, "ha", "MapBiomas Peru C4, Zona de amortiguamiento")
```

## Gold price (World Bank), exchange rate and prices in Peru (BCRP)

```{r prices-read}
pink <- read_excel(file.path(RAW, "CMO-Historical-Data-Monthly.xlsx"), sheet = "Monthly Prices", skip = 4) %>%
  rename(month = 1) %>% filter(grepl("^\\d{4}M\\d{2}$", month)) %>%
  transmute(date = as.Date(paste0(substr(month, 1, 4), "-", substr(month, 6, 7), "-01")),
            gold_usd = as.numeric(Gold))

es <- c(Ene = 1, Feb = 2, Mar = 3, Abr = 4, May = 5, Jun = 6, Jul = 7, Ago = 8, Sep = 9, Oct = 10, Nov = 11, Dic = 12)
read_bcrp <- function(code, name) {
  j <- fromJSON(file.path(RAW, paste0("bcrp_", code, ".json")))
  tibble(period = j$periods$name, value = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(unlist(j$periods$values)))) %>%
    transmute(date = as.Date(sprintf("%s-%02d-01", substr(period, 5, 8), es[substr(period, 1, 3)])),
              !!name := value)
}
fx  <- read_bcrp("PN01234PM", "pen_per_usd")   # soles per US dollar, monthly average
cpi <- read_bcrp("PN38705PM", "cpi_lima")      # Lima consumer price index, Dec 2021 = 100

check("World Bank Pink Sheet: gold, August 2026 (USD per oz)", pink$gold_usd[pink$date == as.Date("2026-08-01")], 4411)
check("BCRP website: exchange rate, September 2026 (soles per USD)", fx$pen_per_usd[fx$date == as.Date("2026-09-01")], pub("bcrp_fx_sep2026"), tol = 0.0001)
log_number("gold_aug2026", "Gold price, August 2026", pink$gold_usd[pink$date == as.Date("2026-08-01")], "USD per oz", "World Bank Pink Sheet, Oct 2026 vintage")
```

## Amazon Mining Watch and official boundaries

Amazon Mining Watch publishes two products. We use both.

- **Detections**: squares of about 480 m by 480 m (about 23 ha) where a
  computer model first sees mining. We count them as "patches".
- **Scar map**: a map with 10 m pixels. Each mining pixel carries the
  period when it was first mapped as mining. We add up the pixels to get
  **hectares**. Amazon Mining Watch says this map is still "in
  development" and that areas "run large" compared with areas drawn by
  hand. So we trust **changes between periods** more than any single
  total.

Boundaries: GADM for departments; SERNANP for protected areas, buffer
zones and titled native communities; INGEMMET (through SERNANP's map
service) for mining concessions that are titled or in process.

```{r amw-read}
amw <- st_read(amw_file, quiet = TRUE)
gadm_path <- paste0("/vsizip/", normalizePath(file.path(RAW, "gadm41_PER_1.json.zip")), "/gadm41_PER_1.json")
dep1 <- st_read(gadm_path, quiet = TRUE)
mdd_poly <- dep1 %>% filter(NAME_1 == "MadredeDios")
anp <- st_read(file.path(RAW, "sernanp_anp_nacional_peru.geojson"), quiet = TRUE)
za  <- st_read(file.path(RAW, "sernanp_zona_amortiguamiento_peru.geojson"), quiet = TRUE)
cn  <- st_read(file.path(RAW, "sernanp_comunidades_nativas.geojson"), quiet = TRUE)
conc <- bind_rows(st_read(file.path(RAW, "ingemmet_concessions_layer36.geojson"), quiet = TRUE),
                  st_read(file.path(RAW, "ingemmet_concessions_layer37.geojson"), quiet = TRUE))
anp_v <- st_make_valid(anp); za_v <- st_make_valid(za); cn_v <- st_make_valid(cn); conc_v <- st_make_valid(conc)

# Each detection is a ~480 m square. Reduce it to its centre point.
# "category" is exclusive, with a priority order: protected area > buffer zone > native community > rest.
pts <- suppressWarnings(st_centroid(amw))
pts <- pts[lengths(st_intersects(pts, mdd_poly)) > 0, ]
inside <- function(p, poly) lengths(st_intersects(p, poly)) > 0
pts <- pts %>% mutate(
  category = case_when(inside(., anp_v) ~ "Protected area",
                       inside(., za_v)  ~ "Buffer zone",
                       inside(., cn_v)  ~ "Native community",
                       TRUE ~ "Rest of Madre de Dios"),
  period = case_when(grepl("^Q", onset) ~ paste0("20", substr(onset, 3, 4), " Q", substr(onset, 2, 2)),
                     TRUE ~ onset))
cat("Detections in Madre de Dios:", nrow(pts), "of", nrow(amw), "in the Amazon basin\n")
log_number("amw_mdd_n", "Amazon Mining Watch detections in Madre de Dios (all periods)", nrow(pts), "patches", "Amazon Mining Watch, README dated 3 Oct 2026")
```

**Checks for the detections file.** These two checks stop the notebook
if a new download differs from the version we used (the number of
detections in the file, and the number in Peru first seen in 2024). The
public dashboard shows hectares, not detections, so we check the
dashboard against the scar map below.

```{r amw-check}
peru_poly <- st_union(dep1)
amw_pts_all <- suppressWarnings(st_centroid(amw))
peru_2024 <- sum(lengths(st_intersects(amw_pts_all[amw_pts_all$onset == "2024", ], peru_poly)) > 0)
check("Amazon Mining Watch: features in the basin file (version of 3 Oct 2026)", nrow(amw), 232030, tol = 0.5)
check("Amazon Mining Watch: Peru, first detected in 2024 (patches)", peru_2024, 2072, tol = 0.5)
log_number("amw_peru_2024", "AMW detections in Peru with onset 2024 (version check)", peru_2024, "patches", "Amazon Mining Watch GeoJSON")
```

**From the scar map to hectares.** The map covers the whole Amazon and is
almost empty, so we read only the tiles (1,024 by 1,024 pixels) that
contain a detection in Peru. Each mining pixel gets the zones that
contain its centre: department, protected area, buffer zone, native
community, mining concession. Then we add up the pixel areas. This takes
about one minute.

```{r scar-hectares}
scar_r <- rast(scar_file)
amw_pe <- amw[lengths(st_intersects(amw, st_buffer(peru_poly, 0.01))) > 0, ]
px <- res(scar_r)[1]; x0 <- xmin(scar_r); y0 <- ymax(scar_r); B <- 1024 * px
bb <- t(sapply(st_geometry(amw_pe), function(g) as.numeric(st_bbox(g))))
m <- 0.01                                            # margin of about 1 km around each detection
tiles <- unique(bind_rows(
  tibble(c = floor((bb[, 1] - m - x0) / B), r = floor((y0 - bb[, 4] - m) / B)),
  tibble(c = floor((bb[, 3] + m - x0) / B), r = floor((y0 - bb[, 4] - m) / B)),
  tibble(c = floor((bb[, 1] - m - x0) / B), r = floor((y0 - bb[, 2] + m) / B)),
  tibble(c = floor((bb[, 3] + m - x0) / B), r = floor((y0 - bb[, 2] + m) / B))))

dep_names <- recode(dep1$NAME_1, MadredeDios = "Madre de Dios", SanMartín = "San Martín")
DEP <- vect(dep1); DEP$id <- seq_len(nrow(DEP))
zone_layers <- list(
  tamb_res = anp_v %>% filter(anp_nomb == "Tambopata"),
  anp_any  = anp_v,
  za_tb    = za_v %>% filter(grepl("Tambopata|Bahuaja-Sonene", anp_nomb)),   # shared buffer counted once, as Tambopata
  za_am    = za_v %>% filter(grepl("Amarakaeri", anp_nomb)),
  za_sira  = za_v %>% filter(grepl("Sira", anp_nomb)),
  za_any   = za_v,
  cn       = cn_v,
  conc     = conc_v) %>% map(vect)

scar_parts <- list()
for (k in seq_len(nrow(tiles))) {
  e <- ext(x0 + tiles$c[k] * B, x0 + (tiles$c[k] + 1) * B, y0 - (tiles$r[k] + 1) * B, y0 - tiles$r[k] * B)
  rb <- crop(scar_r, e); v <- values(rb, mat = FALSE); i <- which(!is.na(v) & v > 0)
  if (!length(i)) next
  d <- tibble(code = v[i], ha = values(cellSize(rb, unit = "ha"), mat = FALSE)[i])
  dv <- crop(DEP, e)
  d$dep <- if (nrow(dv)) values(rasterize(dv, rb, field = "id"), mat = FALSE)[i] else NA_integer_
  for (nm in names(zone_layers)) {
    lv <- crop(zone_layers[[nm]], e)
    d[[nm]] <- if (nrow(lv)) !is.na(values(rasterize(lv, rb, field = 1), mat = FALSE)[i]) else FALSE
  }
  scar_parts[[length(scar_parts) + 1]] <- d %>% group_by(across(-ha)) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha), pixels = n(), .groups = "drop")
}
scar <- bind_rows(scar_parts) %>% group_by(across(-c(ha, pixels))) %>%
  summarise(ha = sum(ha), pixels = sum(pixels), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(dep)) %>%                                                   # keep pixels inside Peru
  mutate(department = dep_names[dep],
         period = if_else(code < 3000, as.character(code), paste0(substr(code, 1, 4), " Q", substr(code, 5, 5))),
         mdd = department == "Madre de Dios",
         title = case_when(anp_any ~ "1 Protected area",
                           za_any & !conc ~ "2 Buffer zone, no mining title",
                           !conc ~ "3 Elsewhere, no mining title",
                           TRUE ~ "4 Inside a mining concession"))
write_csv(scar, file.path(OUT, "table_scar_hectares_by_zone.csv"))

# Check against Amazon Mining Watch's own table of hectares (same release, published 5 Oct 2026)
jur <- read_csv(file.path(RAW, "amw_mined_areas_by_jurisdiction.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
jur_pe   <- sum(jur$intersected_area_ha[jur$type == "national_admin" & jur$country_code %in% "PE"])
jur_tamb <- sum(jur$intersected_area_ha[jur$type == "protected_areas" & jur$name == "Tambopata"])
check("AMW scar map: Peru, all periods (ha; within 0.1%)", sum(scar$ha), jur_pe, tol = 0.001 * jur_pe)
check("AMW scar map: Tambopata National Reserve, all periods (ha; within 1%)", sum(scar$ha[scar$tamb_res]), jur_tamb, tol = 0.01 * jur_tamb)
# Check against the public dashboard (amazonminingwatch.org), which shows hectares up to 2026 Q2
upto_q2 <- scar$code != 20263
check("AMW dashboard: Peru, until 2026 Q2 (ha; dashboard rounds to 0.1k)", sum(scar$ha[upto_q2]), pub("amw_dash_peru"), tol = 100)
check("AMW dashboard: Tambopata National Reserve, until 2026 Q2 (ha; within 1%)", sum(scar$ha[upto_q2 & scar$tamb_res]), pub("amw_dash_tamb"), tol = 0.01 * pub("amw_dash_tamb"))
log_number("scar_peru_all", "AMW new scar, Peru, all periods 2018 to 2026 Q3", sum(scar$ha), "ha", "AMW scar map (our sum)")
log_number("scar_peru_all_amw", "AMW new scar, Peru, all periods, AMW's own table", jur_pe, "ha", "AMW mined_areas_by_jurisdiction.csv")
```

# What happened in Madre de Dios

The MapBiomas tables give a **stock**: all land classified as mining in
a year. The stock rarely goes down, so it rises over time almost
whatever happens. We therefore use **flows**. The transition sheet tells
us how much land **came into** mining each year, and from which class
(forest, water, beach, other), and how much **left** mining.

```{r describe-table}
flows <- tr_mdd %>% filter(year >= 2001) %>%
  mutate(origin = case_when(class_from %in% FOREST ~ "from_forest",
                            class_from %in% WATER  ~ "from_water",
                            class_from == BEACH    ~ "from_beach",
                            TRUE                   ~ "from_other")) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(gross_in   = sum(ha[class_to == MINING & class_from != MINING]),
            from_forest = sum(ha[class_to == MINING & origin == "from_forest"]),
            from_water  = sum(ha[class_to == MINING & origin == "from_water"]),
            from_beach  = sum(ha[class_to == MINING & origin == "from_beach"]),
            from_other  = sum(ha[class_to == MINING & origin == "from_other" & class_from != MINING]),
            gross_out   = sum(ha[class_from == MINING & class_to != MINING]),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(mdd_level, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(net_addition = mining_ha - lag(mining_ha))
flows$net_addition[flows$year == 2001] <- mdd_level$mining_ha[mdd_level$year == 2001] - mdd_level$mining_ha[mdd_level$year == 2000]

stopifnot(all(abs(flows$gross_in - flows$gross_out - flows$net_addition) < 1))   # flows add up

for (y in 2021:2023) check(paste("Net addition, Madre de Dios,", y, "(ha, Q5 card)"),
                           flows$net_addition[flows$year == y], c(`2021` = 4940, `2022` = 10540, `2023` = 19339)[as.character(y)])

flows %>% filter(year >= 2014) %>%
  transmute(Year = year, `Stock (ha)` = fmt(mining_ha), `Net addition` = fmt(net_addition),
            `Came in` = fmt(gross_in), `from forest` = fmt(from_forest), `from water` = fmt(from_water),
            `from beaches` = fmt(from_beach), `from other land` = fmt(from_other), `Left mining` = fmt(gross_out)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Madre de Dios, MapBiomas Peru Collection 4: mining stock and flows (ha)", align = "r")
write_csv(flows, file.path(OUT, "table1_mdd_mining_flows.csv"))
```

```{r describe-numbers, include = FALSE}
f <- function(y, v) flows[[v]][flows$year == y]
share_water_2023 <- f(2023, "from_water") / f(2023, "gross_in")
log_number("net_2021", "Net addition, Madre de Dios, 2021", f(2021, "net_addition"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4")
log_number("net_2022", "Net addition, Madre de Dios, 2022", f(2022, "net_addition"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4")
log_number("net_2023", "Net addition, Madre de Dios, 2023", f(2023, "net_addition"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4")
log_number("net_2024", "Net addition, Madre de Dios, 2024", f(2024, "net_addition"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4")
log_number("net_2025", "Net addition, Madre de Dios, 2025", f(2025, "net_addition"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4")
for (y in 2021:2025) log_number(paste0("ff_", y), paste("Forest to mining, Madre de Dios,", y), f(y, "from_forest"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
log_number("water_2022", "Water to mining, Madre de Dios, 2022", f(2022, "from_water"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
log_number("water_2023", "Water to mining, Madre de Dios, 2023", f(2023, "from_water"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
log_number("water_2024", "Water to mining, Madre de Dios, 2024", f(2024, "from_water"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
log_number("share_water_2023", "Share of land coming into mining that was water, 2023", 100 * share_water_2023, "%", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
log_number("gross_in_2025", "Land coming into mining, Madre de Dios, 2025", f(2025, "gross_in"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
log_number("gross_out_2024", "Land leaving mining, Madre de Dios, 2024", f(2024, "gross_out"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
log_number("gross_out_2025", "Land leaving mining, Madre de Dios, 2025", f(2025, "gross_out"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
log_number("gross_out_2001_2025", "Land leaving mining, Madre de Dios, 2001 to 2025 (a pixel can count more than once)", sum(flows$gross_out[flows$year >= 2001]), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
log_number("share_mdd_amazon", "Madre de Dios share of mining area in Peru's Amazon biome, 2025", 100 * f(2025, "mining_ha") / amazon_2025, "%", "MapBiomas C4")
```

We describe Madre de Dios because it holds
`r round(100 * f(2025, "mining_ha") / amazon_2025)`% of the mining land
in Peru's Amazon (2025).

**[Description]** The net addition (stock this year minus stock last
year) more than doubled in 2022 (`r fmt(f(2022,"net_addition"))` ha, up
from `r fmt(f(2021,"net_addition"))` ha) and almost doubled again in
2023 (`r fmt(f(2023,"net_addition"))` ha). But the flows show that much
of the 2023 jump was not new forest loss. In 2023,
`r fmt(f(2023,"from_water"))` ha that came into mining had been **water**
the year before (`r round(100*share_water_2023)`% of all land coming
in). In 2022 it was `r fmt(f(2022,"from_water"))` ha, and in 2024
`r fmt(f(2024,"from_water"))` ha. Forest that became mining grew more
slowly: `r fmt(f(2021,"from_forest"))`, `r fmt(f(2022,"from_forest"))`
and `r fmt(f(2023,"from_forest"))` ha in 2021, 2022 and 2023.

**Why would water become mining?** Old mining pits fill with water and
the map then calls them water. If miners come back, or if the map
changes its mind, the same land is called mining again. Mining can also
move into river channels. The map cannot tell these stories apart
**[Interpretation, not tested]**. We think the way the map is made
explains a large part of it, for two reasons. First, studies in Madre de
Dios show that satellite methods find mining ponds hard to classify: the
water in active ponds is muddy, and ponds change colour as they age
(Caballero Espejo et al. 2018; Camalan et al. 2022). Second, water to
mining also jumped in the rest of Peru in 2023 (Section 10), and miners
going back to old pits in Madre de Dios cannot explain that. **So what
did we decide?** Our yearly indicator (KPI 4) counts only **forest that
became mining**, not the net addition. Trees turning into bare ground
are much easier to see from space than a pond turning into mining.

```{r fig-flows, fig.height = 4.5}
flows %>% filter(year >= 2010) %>%
  select(year, `Forest` = from_forest, `Rivers and water` = from_water, `Beaches` = from_beach, `Other cleared land` = from_other) %>%
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "origin", values_to = "ha") %>%
  mutate(origin = factor(origin, levels = c("Other cleared land", "Beaches", "Rivers and water", "Forest"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, ha, fill = origin)) + geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = filter(flows, year >= 2010), aes(year, net_addition), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Forest" = col_main, "Rivers and water" = "#5DADE2", "Beaches" = "#F5CBA7", "Other cleared land" = col_grey)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2025, 3)) +
  labs(title = "Madre de Dios: where new mining land came from each year",
       subtitle = "Bars: land that came into mining, by what it was the year before. White dots: net addition (change in the stock).",
       x = NULL, y = "ha per year", fill = NULL,
       caption = "Source: MapBiomas Peru, Collection 4, TRANSITION_4 sheet (Limites politicos), class 30 Minería.")
ggsave(file.path(OUT, "fig_flows_by_origin.png"), width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```

The next chart shows one year as steps: the 2024 stock, plus what came
in, minus what left, gives the 2025 stock.

```{r fig-waterfall, fig.height = 4}
w <- flows %>% filter(year == 2025)
wf <- tibble(step = c("Stock 2024", "+ from forest", "+ from water", "+ from beaches", "+ from other land", "left mining", "Stock 2025"),
             delta = c(mdd_level$mining_ha[mdd_level$year == 2024], w$from_forest, w$from_water, w$from_beach, w$from_other, -w$gross_out, NA)) %>%
  mutate(end = cumsum(replace_na(delta, 0)), start = lag(end, default = 0),
         start = if_else(step == "Stock 2025", 0, start), end = if_else(step == "Stock 2025", lag(end), end),
         type = case_when(step %in% c("Stock 2024", "Stock 2025") ~ "stock", delta < 0 ~ "out", TRUE ~ "in"),
         step = factor(step, step), label = fmt(abs(end - start)))
ggplot(wf, aes(x = step)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = as.numeric(step) - 0.4, xmax = as.numeric(step) + 0.4, ymin = start, ymax = end, fill = type)) +
  geom_text(aes(y = pmax(start, end), label = label), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(stock = col_grey, `in` = col_main, out = col_soft), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(90000, 125000)) +
  labs(title = "From the 2024 stock to the 2025 stock in Madre de Dios (ha)",
       subtitle = paste0("Net addition (", fmt(w$net_addition), " ha) = land that came in (", fmt(w$gross_in),
                         " ha) minus land that left (", fmt(w$gross_out), " ha)"),
       x = NULL, y = "ha", caption = "Source: MapBiomas Peru, Collection 4, TRANSITION_4. Note: the vertical axis starts at 90,000 ha.")
ggsave(file.path(OUT, "fig_waterfall_2025.png"), width = 9, height = 4, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```

## What old mining became

The same transition sheet tells us what land became when it **left**
mining (rows with `class_from = 30`).

```{r left-mining}
left_to <- tr_mdd %>% filter(class_from == MINING, class_to != MINING, year >= 2016) %>%
  mutate(to = case_when(class_to %in% FOREST ~ "Forest (regrowth)",
                        class_to == 21       ~ "Farmland or pasture",
                        class_to == BEACH    ~ "River beach",
                        class_to %in% c(11, 51) ~ "Flooded grassland",
                        class_to %in% WATER  ~ "Water (flooded pits, rivers)",
                        TRUE                 ~ "Other (bare land, urban)")) %>%
  group_by(year, to) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop")
lt25 <- left_to %>% filter(year == 2025) %>% mutate(share = 100 * ha / sum(ha)) %>% arrange(desc(ha))
knitr::kable(lt25 %>% transmute(`Mining land in 2024 that became...` = to, `ha in 2025` = fmt(ha), `Share (%)` = round(share)),
             caption = "Madre de Dios: what land that left mining in 2025 became (MapBiomas Peru C4, TRANSITION_4)")
write_csv(left_to, file.path(OUT, "table1b_mining_left_to.csv"))
lt <- function(x) lt25$share[lt25$to == x]
for (x in lt25$to) log_number(paste0("left_", gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(x))), paste("Share of land leaving mining in 2025 that became:", x), lt(x), "%", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
m2w_2122 <- sum(left_to$ha[left_to$to == "Water (flooded pits, rivers)" & left_to$year %in% 2021:2022])
log_number("mining_to_water_2122", "Mining land relabelled as water, Madre de Dios, 2021 and 2022", m2w_2122, "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
```

```{r fig-left-mining, fig.height = 3.8}
ggplot(left_to, aes(year, ha, fill = to)) + geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Forest (regrowth)" = "#27AE60", "Farmland or pasture" = "#A0522D", "River beach" = "#F5CBA7",
                               "Flooded grassland" = "#C8D96F", "Water (flooded pits, rivers)" = "#5DADE2", "Other (bare land, urban)" = col_grey), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2016:2025) +
  labs(title = "Madre de Dios: what land leaving mining became each year",
       x = NULL, y = "ha per year", caption = "Source: MapBiomas Peru, Collection 4, TRANSITION_4 (rows with class_from = 30, Minería).")
ggsave(file.path(OUT, "fig_left_mining.png"), width = 9, height = 3.8, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```

**[Description]** In 2025, `r fmt(sum(lt25$ha))` ha left mining:
`r round(lt("Forest (regrowth)"))`% became forest again,
`r round(lt("Farmland or pasture"))`% farmland or pasture,
`r round(lt("River beach"))`% river beach,
`r round(lt("Flooded grassland"))`% flooded grassland and
`r round(lt("Water (flooded pits, rivers)"))`% water. These are
different stories on the ground: an old mine growing back as young,
poor forest; people farming old mining land; a river covering a mined
bank; a pit filling with water. Some changes are also the map changing
its mind about pixels at the edges. So "left mining" does **not** mean
the damage was repaired. The water line also shows the back and forth
behind the 2023 jump: `r fmt(m2w_2122)` ha of mining land was labelled
water in 2021 and 2022, and `r fmt(f(2023, "from_water"))` ha of water
was labelled mining in 2023.

## Three ways to count "new mining"

Different sources count different things. We put three yearly counts for
Madre de Dios side by side. They answer different questions, so we never
subtract one from another.

```{r three-counts}
scar_mdd_year <- scar %>% filter(mdd, code %in% 2019:2024) %>% group_by(year = code) %>% summarise(scar_ha = sum(ha))
three_counts <- flows %>% filter(year %in% 2019:2024) %>% select(year, from_forest, net_addition) %>%
  left_join(scar_mdd_year, "year")
knitr::kable(three_counts %>% transmute(Year = year, `Forest that became mining (MapBiomas)` = fmt(from_forest),
                                        `Net addition to the mining stock (MapBiomas)` = fmt(net_addition),
                                        `Land seen as mining for the first time since 2018 (AMW scar map)` = fmt(scar_ha)),
             caption = "Madre de Dios: three yearly counts of new mining (ha)")
write_csv(three_counts, file.path(OUT, "table2b_three_counts.csv"))
cum_forest_to_mining <- sum(tr_mdd$ha[tr_mdd$class_to == MINING & tr_mdd$class_from %in% FOREST])
log_number("cum_ff", "Cumulative forest to mining, Madre de Dios, 1985 to 2025", cum_forest_to_mining, "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
for (y in 2021:2023) log_number(paste0("scar_mdd_", y), paste("AMW new scar, Madre de Dios,", y), three_counts$scar_ha[three_counts$year == y], "ha", "AMW scar map (our sum)")
```

**[Description]** The Amazon Mining Watch count stays almost flat:
`r fmt(min(three_counts$scar_ha))` to `r fmt(max(three_counts$scar_ha))`
ha a year in 2019 to 2024, and 2022 was its *lowest* year. In the same
years the MapBiomas net addition jumped. The reason is what each one
counts. Amazon Mining Watch counts a piece of land only **the first
time** it is seen as mining. Mining again in an old pit, or a flooded pit
that is mapped as mining again, is not new for Amazon Mining Watch, but
it is new for the MapBiomas stock. **This supports our reading of 2023:
much of the surge happened on land that was already mined before.** It
also tells us how to use Amazon Mining Watch: it is good at showing
mining that reaches **new places**, not at measuring the total amount of
mining.

Two cumulative numbers are also often quoted. MapBiomas, summed over all
years, gives `r fmt(cum_forest_to_mining)` ha of forest turned into
mining in Madre de Dios since 1985. MAAP reports
`r fmt(pub("maap233_mdd"))` ha of mining deforestation up to mid 2025
(MAAP #233). MAAP joins several methods and image sources, so the two
numbers differ for good reasons.

## Buffer zones compared with the rest of Madre de Dios

Two groups and two periods: the buffer zones of protected areas in Madre
de Dios, and the rest of the department; before the surge (2016 to 2020)
and during and after it (2021 to 2025).

```{r compare}
za_mdd <- cov_za %>% filter(department == "Madre de Dios", class == MINING) %>%
  group_by(year) %>% summarise(za = sum(ha), .groups = "drop")
anp_mdd <- cov_anp %>% filter(department == "Madre de Dios", class == MINING) %>%
  group_by(year) %>% summarise(anp = sum(ha), .groups = "drop")
area_za  <- cov_za  %>% filter(department == "Madre de Dios", year == 2025) %>% pull(ha) %>% sum()
area_anp <- cov_anp %>% filter(department == "Madre de Dios", year == 2025) %>% pull(ha) %>% sum()
area_mdd <- cov_pol %>% filter(department == "Madre de Dios", year == 2025) %>% pull(ha) %>% sum()

zones <- mdd_level %>% left_join(za_mdd, "year") %>% left_join(anp_mdd, "year") %>%
  mutate(rest = mining_ha - za - anp) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(za, anp, rest), names_to = "zone", values_to = "stock") %>%
  group_by(zone) %>% arrange(year) %>% mutate(addition = stock - lag(stock)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(zone = recode(zone, za = "Buffer zones", anp = "Protected areas", rest = "Rest of Madre de Dios"),
         area = case_when(zone == "Buffer zones" ~ area_za, zone == "Protected areas" ~ area_anp,
                          TRUE ~ area_mdd - area_za - area_anp))

four <- zones %>% filter(zone != "Protected areas", year %in% 2016:2025) %>%
  mutate(period = if_else(year <= 2020, "2016 to 2020", "2021 to 2025")) %>%
  group_by(zone, period) %>%
  summarise(mean_addition = mean(addition), per_1000ha = 1000 * mean(addition) / first(area), .groups = "drop")
four %>% transmute(Group = zone, Period = period, `Mean yearly addition (ha)` = fmt(mean_addition),
                   `per 1,000 ha of the group` = fmt(per_1000ha, 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Four numbers: mean yearly net addition to mining land", align = "llrr")
write_csv(four, file.path(OUT, "table2_compare_four_numbers.csv"))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(four))) log_number(paste0("cmp_", i), paste("Mean yearly addition,", four$zone[i], four$period[i]), four$mean_addition[i], "ha/yr", "MapBiomas C4 coverage")
dd <- four %>% select(zone, period, mean_addition) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = mean_addition)
```

```{r fig-compare, fig.height = 3}
ggplot(four, aes(x = per_1000ha, y = zone)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = zone), colour = col_grey, linewidth = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = period), size = 4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = fmt(mean_addition), colour = period), vjust = -1.1, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("2016 to 2020" = col_grey, "2021 to 2025" = col_alert), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(title = "Mean yearly addition to mining, per 1,000 ha of each group", subtitle = "Labels: mean hectares per year",
       x = "ha added per year per 1,000 ha", y = NULL, caption = "Source: MapBiomas Peru, Collection 4 (coverage).")
```

**[Description]** Yearly additions in the buffer zones rose from
`r fmt(dd$"2016 to 2020"[dd$zone=="Buffer zones"])` to
`r fmt(dd$"2021 to 2025"[dd$zone=="Buffer zones"])` ha. In the rest of
the department they rose from
`r fmt(dd$"2016 to 2020"[dd$zone=="Rest of Madre de Dios"])` to
`r fmt(dd$"2021 to 2025"[dd$zone=="Rest of Madre de Dios"])` ha. We
start the second period in 2021 because our card defines the surge as
2021 to 2023, and because 2021 is the first year when forest turned into
mining crossed its red line (KPI 4). The rest of the department faces
the same gold price, roads and weather, so it is a fair comparison. It
is **not** a control group: the buffer zones were drawn around areas
already under pressure, and mining can move between the two groups.

# The five indicators

## KPI 1 (early, monthly): the gold price in soles

**Why.** A miner in Madre de Dios is paid in soles, and buys fuel, food
and labour in soles. So we turn the dollar price into soles and remove
inflation (Lima consumer prices). Then we compare it with its own
average over the **previous 36 months**. When gold is worth much more
than usual, mining pays better, and more people may start mining.

**Red line: the ratio reaches 1.20**, which means 20% above the 3 year
average.

```{r kpi1}
gold <- pink %>% inner_join(fx, "date") %>% inner_join(cpi, "date") %>%
  filter(!is.na(pen_per_usd), !is.na(cpi_lima)) %>% arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(gold_pen = gold_usd * pen_per_usd,
         gold_real_pen = gold_pen / cpi_lima * 100,                         # soles of December 2021
         trailing36 = rollapplyr(lag(gold_real_pen), 36, mean, fill = NA),  # previous 36 months only
         ratio = gold_real_pen / trailing36,
         signal = ratio >= 1.20)
latest <- tail(filter(gold, !is.na(ratio)), 1)
first_signals <- gold %>% filter(signal, date >= as.Date("2016-01-01")) %>%
  mutate(run = cumsum(c(1, diff(as.numeric(date)) > 40))) %>% group_by(run) %>% slice(1) %>% ungroup()
knitr::kable(first_signals %>% transmute(`First month above the red line` = format(date, "%b %Y"),
                                         `Real price (soles of Dec 2021 per oz)` = fmt(gold_real_pen), Ratio = round(ratio, 2)),
             caption = "KPI 1: months when a new period above the red line started (since 2016)")
log_number("k1_latest_ratio", paste("Real gold price in soles / previous 36 month mean,", format(latest$date, "%b %Y")), latest$ratio, "ratio", "Pink Sheet + BCRP")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(first_signals))) log_number(paste0("k1_episode_", i), "KPI 1: first month of a period above the red line (yyyymm)", as.numeric(format(first_signals$date[i], "%Y%m")), "yyyymm", "Pink Sheet + BCRP")
log_number("k1_latest_real", paste("Real gold price, soles of Dec 2021,", format(latest$date, "%b %Y")), latest$gold_real_pen, "S/ per oz", "Pink Sheet + BCRP")
g21 <- gold %>% mutate(y = as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))) %>% group_by(y) %>%
  summarise(usd = mean(gold_usd), real_pen = mean(gold_real_pen), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(chg_usd = 100 * (usd / lag(usd) - 1), chg_real_pen = 100 * (real_pen / lag(real_pen) - 1))
knitr::kable(g21 %>% filter(y %in% 2019:2026) %>% transmute(Year = y, `USD per oz` = fmt(usd), `Change in USD (%)` = round(chg_usd, 1),
                                                           `Real soles per oz` = fmt(real_pen), `Change in real soles (%)` = round(chg_real_pen, 1)),
             caption = "Yearly averages (2026: January to the latest month)")
```

```{r fig-kpi1, fig.height = 3.8}
ggplot(filter(gold, date >= as.Date("2015-01-01")), aes(date, ratio)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = col_grey) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.2, colour = col_alert, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(colour = col_main, linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2015-06-01"), y = 1.23, label = "Red line: 20% above the 3 year average", hjust = 0, size = 3, colour = col_alert) +
  labs(title = "KPI 1: real gold price in soles compared with its previous 3 year average",
       x = NULL, y = "Ratio", caption = "Sources: World Bank Pink Sheet (Oct 2026); BCRP series PN01234PM (soles per USD) and PN38705PM (Lima CPI).")
ggsave(file.path(OUT, "fig_kpi1_gold.png"), width = 9, height = 3.8, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```

**[Description]** In `r format(latest$date, "%B %Y")` the real gold
price in soles was `r round(100*(latest$ratio-1))`% above its average of
the previous three years, so **KPI 1 is red today**. It first crossed
the red line in `r format(first_signals$date[1], "%B %Y")`, before the
2021 to 2023 surge. New periods above the line started in
`r paste(format(first_signals$date, "%b %Y"), collapse = ", ")`.

**What it does not show.** Where mining will happen, or how much. It is
a signal of pressure, not a forecast of hectares.

### Why did mining keep growing when the real price fell in 2022 and 2023?

```{r price-puzzle}
price_y <- gold %>% mutate(year = as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))) %>% filter(year <= 2025) %>%
  group_by(year) %>% summarise(real_pen = mean(gold_real_pen), .groups = "drop")
pz <- flows %>% select(year, from_forest) %>% inner_join(price_y, "year") %>% arrange(year) %>%
  mutate(d_ff = from_forest - lag(from_forest), d_lp = log(real_pen) - log(lag(real_pen)))
lag_cor <- map_dfr(0:3, function(k) {
  d <- pz %>% filter(year >= 2003) %>% mutate(x = lag(d_lp, k)) %>% filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(d_ff))
  ct <- cor.test(d$d_ff, d$x)
  tibble(`Price change measured...` = c("in the same year", "1 year earlier", "2 years earlier", "3 years earlier")[k + 1],
         Correlation = round(unname(ct$estimate), 2), `p value` = round(ct$p.value, 2), Years = nrow(d))
})
knitr::kable(pz %>% filter(year >= 2017) %>% transmute(Year = year, `Real gold price (soles of Dec 2021 per oz)` = fmt(real_pen), `Forest that became mining (ha)` = fmt(from_forest)),
             caption = "Real gold price in soles and forest that became mining, Madre de Dios")
knitr::kable(lag_cor, caption = "Correlation between the yearly change in forest that became mining and the change in the real gold price, 2003 to 2025")
pre <- mean(pz$real_pen[pz$year %in% 2017:2019])
above_pre <- 100 * (mean(pz$real_pen[pz$year %in% 2022:2023]) / pre - 1)
log_number("price_2223_vs_1719", "Real gold price in soles, 2022 and 2023 average vs 2017 to 2019 average", above_pre, "%", "Pink Sheet + BCRP")
log_number("lagcor_1", "Correlation: change in forest to mining vs change in real price one year earlier", lag_cor$Correlation[2], "r", "MapBiomas C4 + Pink Sheet + BCRP")
```

**[Description]** In real soles the gold price fell
`r round(100 * (1 - pz$real_pen[pz$year == 2022] / pz$real_pen[pz$year == 2021]))`%
in 2022 and another
`r round(100 * (1 - pz$real_pen[pz$year == 2023] / pz$real_pen[pz$year == 2022]))`%
in 2023. But it was still `r round(above_pre)`% above its 2017 to 2019
average. Profit depends on the **level** of the price, so mining still
paid very well. The yearly change in forest turned into mining does not
move with the price change of the same year
(r = `r lag_cor$Correlation[1]`). It moves a little with the price
change one and two years earlier (r = `r lag_cor$Correlation[2]` and
`r lag_cor$Correlation[3]`). This fits a **delayed response**: opening a
new site needs machines, workers and access. But with about 20 years of
data these correlations could be chance (p =
`r lag_cor$"p value"[2]` and `r lag_cor$"p value"[3]`). Other things
also changed in those years: COVID 19, weaker enforcement after
Operation Mercurio, and (for the net addition only) the 2023 water
relabelling **[Interpretation, not tested]**. We cannot separate these
causes. This is why KPI 1 is a pressure signal, not a forecast.

## KPI 2 (early, monthly): Peru's gold gap

**Why.** Peru's Central Bank publishes every month how much gold Peru
**exported** and how much gold mines **declared as produced**. If Peru
exports much more gold than it declares, the difference has no declared
origin. Part of it is likely illegal gold that entered the legal chain.
Both numbers come from the same publisher, so the subtraction is fair.

**How we measure it.** We use 12 months at a time (to remove the
seasons): the gap = (exports minus declared production) as a share of
exports.

**Red line: the gap jumps.** The gap has been high since 2017, so a
fixed level would be red every year and tell FZS nothing new. Instead,
the red line is a **jump**: the 12 month gap is more than *X* points
higher than one year earlier. We set *X* the same way as our other
statistical red lines: the average yearly change in calm years (2014 to
2016) plus two standard deviations.

```{r kpi2}
b <- fromJSON(file.path(REG, "bcrp_gold_exports_production.json"))
bm <- tibble(p = b$periods$name, v = b$periods$values) %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(substr(p, 5, 8)), month = es[substr(p, 1, 3)],
         export_t = map_dbl(v, ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x[1]))) * 31.1035 / 1000,   # thousand troy oz -> tonnes (fine gold)
         prod_t   = map_dbl(v, ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x[2]))) / 1e6) %>%          # fine grams -> tonnes
  select(-v, -p) %>% filter(!is.na(export_t), !is.na(prod_t))
gap_y <- bm %>% group_by(year) %>% filter(n() == 12) %>%
  summarise(export_t = sum(export_t), prod_t = sum(prod_t), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(gap_t = export_t - prod_t, gap_pct = 100 * gap_t / export_t, change = gap_pct - lag(gap_pct))
h1_26 <- bm %>% filter(year == 2026, month <= 6) %>% summarise(e = sum(export_t), p = sum(prod_t)) %>% mutate(pct = 100 * (e - p) / e)

# Monthly: 12 month gap, and its change against the same month one year earlier
bm_roll <- bm %>% arrange(year, month) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", year, month)),
         gap12 = 100 * (1 - rollapplyr(prod_t, 12, sum, fill = NA) / rollapplyr(export_t, 12, sum, fill = NA)),
         jump = gap12 - lag(gap12, 12))
calm <- bm_roll %>% filter(year %in% 2014:2016, !is.na(jump))
X <- mean(calm$jump) + 2 * sd(calm$jump)
bm_roll <- bm_roll %>% mutate(signal = jump > X)
episodes <- bm_roll %>% filter(signal %in% TRUE) %>% mutate(run = cumsum(c(1, diff(as.numeric(date)) > 100))) %>%   # one quiet month does not end a period
  group_by(run) %>% summarise(from = min(date), to = max(date), peak = max(jump), .groups = "drop")
gap_latest <- tail(filter(bm_roll, !is.na(jump)), 1)

knitr::kable(gap_y %>% filter(year >= 2012) %>% transmute(Year = year, `Exports (t of fine gold)` = fmt(export_t, 1),
             `Declared production (t)` = fmt(prod_t, 1), `Gap (t)` = fmt(gap_t, 1), `Gap (% of exports)` = fmt(gap_pct, 1),
             `Change on the year before (points)` = fmt(change, 1)),
             caption = "Peru: gold exported minus gold declared as produced, by year (BCRP)")
knitr::kable(episodes %>% transmute(`Red from` = format(from, "%b %Y"), `Red until` = format(to, "%b %Y"), `Largest jump (points)` = round(peak, 1)),
             caption = paste0("KPI 2: periods when the 12 month gap was more than ", round(X, 1), " points above one year earlier"))
write_csv(gap_y, file.path(OUT, "tableR2_peru_gold_gap.csv"))
write_csv(bm_roll, file.path(OUT, "table_kpi2_gold_gap_monthly.csv"))
check("BCRP: Peru gold export minus production gap 2025 (t)", gap_y$gap_t[gap_y$year == 2025], 103.0, tol = 0.1)
log_number("pe_gap_2025_t", "Peru gold exports minus declared production, 2025", gap_y$gap_t[gap_y$year == 2025], "t", "BCRP PN38792BM, RD12978DM")
log_number("pe_gap_2025_pct", "Peru gold gap as share of exports, 2025", gap_y$gap_pct[gap_y$year == 2025], "%", "BCRP")
log_number("pe_gap_2017_pct", "Peru gold gap as share of exports, 2017", gap_y$gap_pct[gap_y$year == 2017], "%", "BCRP")
log_number("pe_gap_h1_2026_pct", "Peru gold gap as share of exports, Jan to Jun 2026", h1_26$pct, "%", "BCRP")
log_number("pe_gap_12m_latest", paste("Peru 12 month gold gap,", format(gap_latest$date, "%b %Y")), gap_latest$gap12, "%", "BCRP")
log_number("pe_gap_jump_latest", paste("Peru 12 month gold gap, change on one year earlier,", format(gap_latest$date, "%b %Y")), gap_latest$jump, "points", "BCRP")
log_number("pe_gap_X", "KPI 2 red line: jump in the 12 month gap (2014 to 2016 mean + 2 SD)", X, "points", "BCRP")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(episodes))) log_number(paste0("pe_gap_episode_", i), "KPI 2: first month of a red period (yyyymm)", as.numeric(format(episodes$from[i], "%Y%m")), "yyyymm", "BCRP")
```

```{r fig-kpi2, fig.height = 5.5}
k2a <- ggplot(filter(bm_roll, date >= as.Date("2013-01-01")), aes(date, gap12)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = as.Date("2021-01-01"), xmax = as.Date("2023-12-31"), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = col_soft, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(colour = col_main, linewidth = 0.9) +
  labs(title = "Share of exported gold that is not in declared production (12 months)", x = NULL, y = "% of exports")
k2b <- ggplot(filter(bm_roll, date >= as.Date("2014-01-01")), aes(date, jump)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = as.Date("2021-01-01"), xmax = as.Date("2023-12-31"), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = col_soft, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_grey) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = X, colour = col_alert, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(colour = col_main, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = filter(bm_roll, signal %in% TRUE), colour = col_alert, size = 1.5) +
  labs(title = paste0("KPI 2: change on one year earlier (points). Red line: ", round(X, 1), " points"),
       x = NULL, y = "points", caption = "Shaded: Madre de Dios surge. Source: BCRP series PN38792BM (exports) and RD12978DM (production). Our calculation.")
(k2a / k2b) & scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y")
ggsave(file.path(OUT, "figR_peru_gold_gap.png"), width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```

**[Description]** Peru exported
`r fmt(gap_y$gap_t[gap_y$year == 2025], 1)` t more gold in 2025 than it
declared as produced: `r round(gap_y$gap_pct[gap_y$year == 2025])`% of
all exported gold. In 2017 it was
`r round(gap_y$gap_pct[gap_y$year == 2017])`%. In January to June 2026
it was `r round(h1_26$pct)`%. (The Instituto Peruano de Economía
publishes a similar estimate: 54% in the first half of 2026, from press
reports.)

The red line is a jump of more than `r round(X, 1)` points. The gap
jumped above it in `r nrow(episodes)` periods:
`r paste0(format(episodes$from, "%b %Y"), " to ", format(episodes$to, "%b %Y"), collapse = " and ")`.
The second period started in
**`r format(episodes$from[nrow(episodes)], "%B %Y")`**, in the first year
of the Madre de Dios surge. BCRP publishes each month about two months
later, so FZS could have seen it in mid 2021. The yearly maps showed the
surge only in March 2023. The first period (2017 and 2018) came without
a surge in forest loss, so the rule can also give a warning that is not
followed by more mining. **Today the gap is high
(`r round(gap_latest$gap12)`% over the 12 months to
`r format(gap_latest$date, "%B %Y")`) but it is not jumping**
(`r sprintf("%+.1f", gap_latest$jump)` points on a year earlier), so
KPI 2 is not red.

**What it does not show.** Where the gold was mined. The gap is
national: it includes Madre de Dios, but also Puno, La Libertad and
other regions, and gold smuggled into Peru from neighbouring countries.
The 2014 to 2016 calm period is our choice, and it has only 36 months
(which overlap, because each one covers 12 months). With another
choice, the red line would move.

## KPI 3 (now, quarterly): new mining in FZS landscapes

**Why.** FZS needs to know **where** mining is happening, and fast.
Amazon Mining Watch updates its data within days after each quarter
ends. We count new mining in hectares (from the scar map) and in patches
(from the detections), in four FZS landscapes in Madre de Dios:

- inside the **Tambopata National Reserve**, where mining is always
  illegal;
- the **Tambopata buffer zone** (it overlaps the Bahuaja-Sonene buffer
  zone; we count the shared land once, as Tambopata);
- the **Amarakaeri buffer zone**;
- **native communities** (all titled communities outside reserves; they
  can overlap buffer zones).

**Red lines.**

- **Inside the reserve:** a quarter with more new mining than the
  largest *whole year* of 2019 to 2024. Some mining appears inside the
  reserve every year, so "any mining" would always be red. We compare
  with the worst year instead.
- **Buffer zones and native communities:** the quarters of this year so
  far have more than **25% more** new mining than the same quarters last
  year. We compare the same quarters because mining is seen mostly in
  the dry season (Q2 and Q3), and Q1 is very cloudy.

```{r kpi3-patches}
# Which protected area, buffer zone and native community each detection falls in.
# We keep ALL names a point falls in (polygons overlap).
names_in <- function(p, poly) sapply(st_intersects(p, poly), function(i) paste(sort(unique(poly$anp_nomb[i])), collapse = "|"))
pts$anp_names <- names_in(pts, anp_v)
pts$za_names  <- names_in(pts, za_v)
pts$in_cn     <- lengths(st_intersects(pts, cn_v)) > 0
pts <- pts %>% mutate(
  tamb_reserve = grepl("Tambopata", anp_names),
  tamb_buffer  = anp_names == "" & grepl("Tambopata|Bahuaja-Sonene", za_names),
  amar_buffer  = anp_names == "" & !tamb_buffer & grepl("Amarakaeri", za_names),
  native_any   = anp_names == "" & in_cn)

amw_tab <- pts %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% filter(period != "2018") %>%   # 2018 = everything already there in the first year
  count(period, category) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = category, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))) %>% arrange(period) %>%
  select(period, any_of(c("Protected area", "Buffer zone", "Native community", "Rest of Madre de Dios")), Total)
write_csv(amw_tab, file.path(OUT, "table3_amw_by_category.csv"))

watch <- c("Tambopata (inside reserve)", "Tambopata buffer zone", "Amarakaeri buffer zone",
           "Native communities (all)", "All Madre de Dios")
flag_long <- pts %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  transmute(period, `Tambopata (inside reserve)` = tamb_reserve, `Tambopata buffer zone` = tamb_buffer,
            `Amarakaeri buffer zone` = amar_buffer, `Native communities (all)` = native_any, `All Madre de Dios` = TRUE) %>%
  pivot_longer(-period, names_to = "landscape", values_to = "flag") %>% filter(flag)
patches_q <- flag_long %>% filter(period != "2018") %>% count(landscape, period) %>%
  complete(landscape = watch, period = unique(pts$period[pts$period != "2018"]), fill = list(n = 0))
```

```{r kpi3-hectares}
ha_long <- scar %>% filter(mdd, period != "2018") %>%
  transmute(period, ha, `Tambopata (inside reserve)` = tamb_res, `Tambopata buffer zone` = !anp_any & za_tb,
            `Amarakaeri buffer zone` = !anp_any & !za_tb & za_am, `Native communities (all)` = !anp_any & cn,
            `All Madre de Dios` = TRUE) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(period, ha), names_to = "landscape", values_to = "flag") %>% filter(flag) %>%
  group_by(landscape, period) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(landscape = watch, period = unique(scar$period[scar$period != "2018"]), fill = list(ha = 0))

# One table: hectares and patches by landscape and period; "Rest of Madre de Dios" = all minus the three landscapes
k3 <- ha_long %>% left_join(patches_q, c("landscape", "period")) %>% mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0))
rest <- k3 %>% group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(ha = ha[landscape == "All Madre de Dios"] - sum(ha[landscape %in% watch[1:3]]),
            n  = n[landscape == "All Madre de Dios"]  - sum(n[landscape %in% watch[1:3]]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(landscape = "Rest of Madre de Dios")
watch6 <- c(watch, "Rest of Madre de Dios")
k3 <- bind_rows(k3, rest) %>% mutate(landscape = factor(landscape, watch6), quarterly = grepl("Q", period))
write_csv(k3, file.path(OUT, "table3b_kpi3_hectares_patches.csv"))

knitr::kable(k3 %>% filter(quarterly) %>% transmute(landscape, period, ha = fmt(ha)) %>%
               pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = ha) %>% arrange(landscape) %>% rename(Landscape = landscape),
             caption = "New mining per quarter, hectares (provisional). Rows overlap: native communities also lie in buffer zones.")
knitr::kable(k3 %>% filter(quarterly) %>% transmute(landscape, period, n) %>%
               pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = n) %>% arrange(landscape) %>% rename(Landscape = landscape),
             caption = "The same, in patches (squares of about 23 ha)")

# Red line inside the reserve: a quarter above the largest whole year 2019 to 2024
res_years <- k3 %>% filter(landscape == "Tambopata (inside reserve)", period %in% as.character(2019:2024))
reserve_base_ha <- max(res_years$ha); reserve_base_n <- max(res_years$n)
reserve_q <- k3 %>% filter(landscape == "Tambopata (inside reserve)", quarterly) %>% arrange(period) %>%
  mutate(red = ha > reserve_base_ha)
first_reserve_red <- reserve_q$period[reserve_q$red][1]

# Red line for buffer zones and native communities: this year so far vs the same quarters last year
q_now  <- paste("2026", c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3")); q_last <- paste("2025", c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3"))
ytd <- k3 %>% group_by(landscape) %>%
  summarise(ha25 = sum(ha[period %in% q_last]), ha26 = sum(ha[period %in% q_now]),
            n25 = sum(n[period %in% q_last]), n26 = sum(n[period %in% q_now]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(change = 100 * (ha26 / ha25 - 1),
         red = case_when(landscape == "Tambopata (inside reserve)" ~ any(reserve_q$red & grepl("2026", reserve_q$period)),
                         landscape %in% watch[2:4] ~ change > 25, TRUE ~ NA))
knitr::kable(ytd %>% transmute(Landscape = landscape, `Q1 to Q3 2025 (ha)` = fmt(ha25), `Q1 to Q3 2026 (ha)` = fmt(ha26),
                               `Change` = pct(change), `Patches 2025` = fmt(n25), `Patches 2026` = fmt(n26),
                               `Red?` = if_else(is.na(red), "no red line", if_else(red, "RED", "no"))),
             caption = "KPI 3 today: the first three quarters of 2026 against the same quarters of 2025")
write_csv(ytd, file.path(OUT, "table3c_kpi3_today.csv"))

yv <- function(l, v) ytd[[v]][ytd$landscape == l]
res25 <- sum(k3$ha[k3$landscape == "Tambopata (inside reserve)" & grepl("^2025", k3$period)])
log_number("k3_res_ha_2025", "AMW new scar inside Tambopata National Reserve, 2025 (4 provisional quarters)", res25, "ha", "AMW scar map + SERNANP")
log_number("k3_res_base_ha", "AMW new scar inside Tambopata National Reserve, largest whole year 2019 to 2024", reserve_base_ha, "ha", "AMW scar map + SERNANP")
log_number("k3_res_base_n", "AMW detections inside Tambopata National Reserve, largest whole year 2019 to 2024", reserve_base_n, "patches", "AMW + SERNANP")
log_number("k3_res_q2_2026", "AMW new scar inside Tambopata National Reserve, 2026 Q2 (provisional)", reserve_q$ha[reserve_q$period == "2026 Q2"], "ha", "AMW scar map + SERNANP")
log_number("k3_first_red", "KPI 3 reserve red line first crossed (yyyyq)", as.numeric(gsub(" Q", "", first_reserve_red)), "yyyyq", "AMW scar map + SERNANP")
for (l in watch6) {
  id <- gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(l))
  log_number(paste0("k3_ha25_", id), paste("AMW new scar,", l, "Q1 to Q3 2025"), yv(l, "ha25"), "ha", "AMW scar map + SERNANP")
  log_number(paste0("k3_ha26_", id), paste("AMW new scar,", l, "Q1 to Q3 2026"), yv(l, "ha26"), "ha", "AMW scar map + SERNANP")
  log_number(paste0("k3_n25_", id), paste("AMW detections,", l, "Q1 to Q3 2025"), yv(l, "n25"), "patches", "AMW + SERNANP")
  log_number(paste0("k3_n26_", id), paste("AMW detections,", l, "Q1 to Q3 2026"), yv(l, "n26"), "patches", "AMW + SERNANP")
  log_number(paste0("k3_chg_", id), paste("AMW new scar,", l, "Q1 to Q3 2026 vs 2025"), yv(l, "change"), "%", "AMW scar map + SERNANP")
}
```

**[Description]** In the first three quarters of 2026, Amazon Mining
Watch mapped **`r fmt(yv("Tambopata (inside reserve)", "ha26"))` ha of
new mining inside the Tambopata National Reserve**
(`r yv("Tambopata (inside reserve)", "n26")` patches), against
`r fmt(yv("Tambopata (inside reserve)", "ha25"))` ha
(`r yv("Tambopata (inside reserve)", "n25")` patches) in the same
quarters of 2025. In 2019 to 2024 the most in any whole year was
`r fmt(reserve_base_ha)` ha. The reserve red line was first crossed in
**`r first_reserve_red`**, and it has been red in
`r sum(reserve_q$red)` of the `r nrow(reserve_q)` quarters since. New
mining also rose in the Tambopata buffer zone
(`r pct(yv("Tambopata buffer zone", "change"))`), the Amarakaeri buffer
zone (`r pct(yv("Amarakaeri buffer zone", "change"))`) and native
communities (`r pct(yv("Native communities (all)", "change"))`), so
all three are red. In the rest of Madre de Dios the change was
`r pct(yv("Rest of Madre de Dios", "change"))`.

**Is it real?** For 2025, yes, as far as we can check: Amazon Mining
Watch gives `r fmt(res25)` ha inside the reserve, and MAAP #241 (Amazon
Conservation, 12 May 2026), using very sharp 0.5 m images, reports more
than `r pub("maap241_2025")` ha of mining deforestation inside the
reserve in 2025, with `r pub("maap241_struct")` mining structures and
`r pub("maap241_camps")` camps by February 2026. This is an independent
source.

**For 2026, the evidence is good but less direct.**

- Amazon Mining Watch's own newsletter reports
  `r pub("amw_panorama_h1")` ha of new mining in the reserve in the
  first half of 2026. Our number is
  `r fmt(sum(reserve_q$ha[reserve_q$period %in% c("2026 Q1", "2026 Q2")]))`
  ha. This only shows that we read the data correctly (same source).
- Global Conservation, a different organisation with its own satellite
  monitoring, says the area with illegal mining activity inside the
  reserve grew to about `r fmt(pub("gc_tamb_area"))` ha between October
  2025 and June 2026 (quoted by Mongabay Latam, 27 September 2026).
  Amazon Mining Watch gives
  `r fmt(sum(reserve_q$ha[reserve_q$period %in% c("2025 Q4", "2026 Q1", "2026 Q2")]))`
  ha for the same nine months. The two measure slightly different
  things, but they agree on the size. **So the 2026 Q2 jump is supported
  by an independent source.**
- For 2026 Q3 the picture is unclear. SERNANP's radar system (RAMI)
  found only `r pub("rami_tamb_julaug")` ha of forest lost inside the
  reserve in July and August 2026 (same article), while Amazon Mining
  Watch shows `r fmt(reserve_q$ha[reserve_q$period == "2026 Q3"])` ha in
  Q3. RAMI counts only forest that is lost, while Amazon Mining Watch
  counts any land seen as mining for the first time (also river banks
  and land cleared before), so the two can differ. FZS should treat
  2026 Q3 as provisional.

**A note on hectares and patches.** A patch counts each 480 m square
once, however little of it is mined. Hectares measure the mined area.
Both tell the same story here, and the reserve red line is first crossed
in the same quarter with both. We use hectares as the main number because
they can be compared with MAAP and MapBiomas. Pietro's separate
calculation from the same scar map (pipeline by Pietro Maran) gives the
same hectares. This is a check of our code, not an independent check of
the satellite data.

**How much of it has a mining title?** We use Likitha's four groups,
with the official map of mining concessions (titled or in process):
protected area; buffer zone with no mining title; elsewhere with no
mining title; inside a mining concession. The first three are
"probably illegal".

```{r kpi3-title}
title_mdd <- scar %>% filter(mdd, period != "2018") %>%
  mutate(when = case_when(code %in% 2019:2024 ~ as.character(code), grepl("^2025", period) ~ "2025 (quarters)",
                          period %in% q_now ~ "2026 Q1 to Q3")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(when)) %>% group_by(when, title) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(when) %>% mutate(share = 100 * ha / sum(ha)) %>% ungroup()
title_wide <- title_mdd %>% transmute(when, title, share = round(share)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = title, values_from = share, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(`Probably illegal (groups 1 to 3)` = 100 - `4 Inside a mining concession`)
knitr::kable(title_wide %>% rename(Period = when), caption = "Madre de Dios: share of new mining hectares in each group (%). Today's concession map is used for every year.")
write_csv(title_mdd, file.path(OUT, "table3e_kpi3_mining_title.csv"))
noti <- function(w) 100 - title_wide$`4 Inside a mining concession`[title_wide$when == w]
log_number("k3_notitle_1924", "Share of new mining hectares in Madre de Dios with no mining title, 2019 to 2024 average of yearly shares", mean(sapply(as.character(2019:2024), noti)), "%", "AMW scar map + SERNANP + INGEMMET")
log_number("k3_notitle_2026", "Share of new mining hectares in Madre de Dios with no mining title, 2026 Q1 to Q3", noti("2026 Q1 to Q3"), "%", "AMW scar map + SERNANP + INGEMMET")
```

**[Description]** In 2019 to 2024, about
`r round(mean(sapply(as.character(2019:2024), noti)))`% of new mining
hectares in Madre de Dios had no mining title. In the first three
quarters of 2026 it was `r round(noti("2026 Q1 to Q3"))`%. Two warnings:
we use **today's** concession map for every year (a concession granted
in 2024 makes 2019 mining on that land look titled), and "no title" is
not proof that mining is illegal. Mining inside a concession is not
proof that it is legal either.

### Maps: where the new mining is

```{r maps-setup}
xy <- st_coordinates(pts); pts$x <- xy[, 1]; pts$y <- xy[, 2]
se_box <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(xmin = -72.6, ymin = -13.7, xmax = -68.5, ymax = -9.7), crs = 4326))
zones_sf <- bind_rows(za_v %>% transmute(zone = "Buffer zone"), anp_v %>% transmute(zone = "Protected area"),
                      cn_v %>% transmute(zone = "Native community")) %>%
  filter(lengths(st_intersects(., se_box)) > 0) %>%
  mutate(zone = factor(zone, c("Buffer zone", "Protected area", "Native community")))
map_base <- list(
  geom_sf(data = dep1, fill = "#F4F4F1", colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
  geom_sf(data = mdd_poly, fill = "white", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5),
  geom_sf(data = zones_sf, aes(fill = zone, colour = zone), linewidth = 0.3),
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Buffer zone" = "#E3F1DF", "Protected area" = "#A9D49A", "Native community" = "#EBDDEB"), name = NULL),
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Buffer zone" = "#8DBF83", "Protected area" = "#3E8E41", "Native community" = "#B07AA1"), guide = "none"))
anp_labels <- suppressWarnings(anp_v %>% filter(anp_nomb %in% c("Tambopata", "Amarakaeri", "Bahuaja-Sonene", "del Manu", "Alto Purús")) %>%
  group_by(anp_nomb) %>% summarise() %>% st_intersection(st_geometry(mdd_poly)) %>% st_point_on_surface())
zx <- c(-70.8, -68.95); zy <- c(-13.3, -12.2)
pp <- st_drop_geometry(pts)
```

**[Description]** The share of new patches inside protected areas or
buffer zones rose from `r shift$"share (%)"[shift$when == periods[2]]`%
during the 2021 to 2023 surge to
`r shift$"share (%)"[shift$when == periods[5]]`% in the first three
quarters of 2026. New mining is moving south, towards the Tambopata
buffer zone and reserve.

```{r fig-kpi3, fig.height = 4.2}
k3 %>% filter(quarterly, landscape %in% watch6[c(1:4, 6)]) %>%
  ggplot(aes(period, ha, fill = grepl("2026", period))) + geom_col() +
```

**What it does not show.** Mining again inside old pits (Amazon Mining
Watch counts land only the first time), dredges on rivers (the model
ignores them), and legality. The quarters are provisional and can be
revised. Amazon Mining Watch rebuilt its model in 2026 and replaces its
files, so FZS cannot see what the data said in the past: it should save
a copy every quarter.

## KPI 4 (late, yearly): forest that became mining

**Why.** This is the trusted yearly number for donors. It comes from
MapBiomas Peru, which maps all of Peru every year since 1985. We count
only **forest that became mining**, for the reason explained in Section
4. We show two lines:

- **Inside reserves and buffer zones**: four FZS landscapes (Tambopata,
  Amarakaeri, Bahuaja-Sonene and Manu), inside the reserves and in their
  buffer zones. This includes the parts outside Madre de Dios
  (Bahuaja-Sonene in Puno, part of Amarakaeri in Cusco). Inside a
  reserve mining is always illegal. In a buffer zone it needs SERNANP's
  approval.
- **All of Madre de Dios.**

**Red line: this year is above the average of the previous five years
plus two standard deviations.** This is a standard "control chart" rule:
a value so far above the recent past that normal ups and downs do not
explain it.

```{r kpi4}
control <- function(d) d %>% arrange(year) %>%
  mutate(mean5 = rollapplyr(lag(ha), 5, mean, fill = NA), sd5 = rollapplyr(lag(ha), 5, sd, fill = NA),
         limit = mean5 + 2 * sd5, red = ha > limit)
landscapes <- c("Tambopata", "Amarakaeri", "Bahuaja-Sonene", "del Manu")
ff_by <- function(tr, label) tr %>% filter(unit %in% landscapes, class_to == MINING, class_from %in% FOREST) %>%
  group_by(year) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop") %>% mutate(zone = label)
k4 <- bind_rows(ff_by(tr_anp, "Inside the reserves"), ff_by(tr_za, "Buffer zones"),
                flows %>% transmute(year, ha = from_forest, zone = "All Madre de Dios")) %>%
  filter(year >= 2001) %>% group_by(zone) %>% group_modify(~ control(.x)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(zone = factor(zone, c("Inside the reserves", "Buffer zones", "All Madre de Dios")))
knitr::kable(k4 %>% filter(year >= 2016) %>% transmute(year, zone, txt = paste0(fmt(ha), " (", fmt(limit), ")", if_else(red %in% TRUE, " RED", ""))) %>%
               pivot_wider(names_from = zone, values_from = txt) %>% select(Year = year, all_of(levels(k4$zone))),
             caption = "KPI 4: forest that became mining, ha (red line in brackets). Reserves and buffer zones: Tambopata, Amarakaeri, Bahuaja-Sonene and Manu.")
write_csv(k4, file.path(OUT, "table4_kpi4_forest_to_mining.csv"))
k4v <- function(z, y, v = "ha") k4[[v]][k4$zone == z & k4$year == y]
red_years <- function(z) paste(k4$year[k4$zone == z & k4$red %in% TRUE & k4$year >= 2016], collapse = ", ")
for (z in levels(k4$zone)) {
  id <- c("Inside the reserves" = "res", "Buffer zones" = "za", "All Madre de Dios" = "mdd")[z]
  log_number(paste0("k4_", id, "_2025"), paste("Forest to mining, 2025,", z), k4v(z, 2025), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
  log_number(paste0("k4_", id, "_lim_2025"), paste("KPI 4 red line, 2025,", z), k4v(z, 2025, "limit"), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
}
tamb_in <- cov_anp %>% filter(unit == "Tambopata", department == "Madre de Dios", class == MINING) %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha))
log_number("tamb_anp_2025", "Mining area inside Tambopata National Reserve, 2025", tamb_in$ha[tamb_in$year == 2025], "ha", "MapBiomas C4 ANP")
log_number("tamb_anp_base", "Mining area inside Tambopata National Reserve, mean 2016 to 2020", mean(tamb_in$ha[tamb_in$year %in% 2016:2020]), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 ANP")
```

```{r fig-kpi4, fig.height = 3.8}
ggplot(filter(k4, year >= 2010), aes(year, ha)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = red %in% TRUE)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = limit), colour = col_alert, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~zone, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = col_main, `TRUE` = col_alert), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2025, 5)) +
  labs(title = "KPI 4: forest that became mining (ha per year)",
       subtitle = "Red bars: above the previous 5 year average + 2 standard deviations (dashed line)", x = NULL, y = "ha",
       caption = "Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4, transitions.")
ggsave(file.path(OUT, "fig_kpi4.png"), width = 9, height = 3.8, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```

**[Description]** In 2025, forest that became mining was
**`r fmt(k4v("Inside the reserves", 2025))` ha inside the reserves**
(red line `r fmt(k4v("Inside the reserves", 2025, "limit"))` ha) and
**`r fmt(k4v("Buffer zones", 2025))` ha in their buffer zones** (red
line `r fmt(k4v("Buffer zones", 2025, "limit"))` ha). Both are red. Red
years since 2016: inside the reserves `r red_years("Inside the reserves")`;
buffer zones `r red_years("Buffer zones")`; all of Madre de Dios
`r red_years("All Madre de Dios")`.

**An honest limit of the rule.** In all of Madre de Dios, 2025 was the
**highest year on record**
(`r fmt(k4v("All Madre de Dios", 2025))` ha), but it is **not red**: the
red line was `r fmt(k4v("All Madre de Dios", 2025, "limit"))` ha. The
reason is that the red line uses the previous five years, and those
include the surge years 2021 to 2023. After a surge, the line moves up,
so only a new and even bigger jump is red. We double checked this with a
second, separate calculation (in Python, straight from the MapBiomas
file) and got the same numbers. This is why we **lead with the reserves
and buffer zones line**: it is where FZS acts, and it turned red. FZS
should also report the plain number every year ("highest on record"),
not only the colour.

We report hectares, not the share of all new mining. During the surge
the share inside FZS landscapes *fell* (the surge was mainly elsewhere
in the department), so a share would hide growth inside them. MAAP's
own count for January 2021 to March 2024 (MAAP #208) puts
`r pub("maap208_outside")`% of mining deforestation outside the legal
mining corridor: `r pub("maap208_cn")`% in native communities and
`r pub("maap208_za")`% in buffer zones.

**What it does not show.** Mining in rivers, mining again on old sites,
mercury. It arrives late: each year's map is published 5 to 17 months
after the year ends. MapBiomas also revises earlier years in each new
version (Section 10).

## KPI 5 (now, quarterly): is mining spreading outside Madre de Dios?

**Why.** If FZS only watches Madre de Dios, it can miss a new mining
front somewhere else in Peru. KPI 5 adds up new mining in **all of Peru
outside Madre de Dios**, from the same scar map as KPI 3.

**Red line:** the same as for buffer zones in KPI 3: this year so far
has more than 25% more new mining than the same quarters last year.

```{r kpi5}
out_mdd <- scar %>% filter(!mdd, period != "2018") %>%
  mutate(when = case_when(code %in% 2019:2024 ~ as.character(code), grepl("^2025", period) ~ "2025",
                          grepl("^2026", period) ~ "2026 (Q1 to Q3)"))
k5_dep <- out_mdd %>% group_by(department, when) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(department) %>% filter(sum(ha) >= 100) %>% ungroup()
k5_tot <- out_mdd %>% group_by(when) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop") %>% mutate(department = "Total outside Madre de Dios")
knitr::kable(bind_rows(k5_dep, k5_tot) %>% mutate(ha = fmt(ha)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = when, values_from = ha, values_fill = "0") %>%
               rename(Department = department),
             caption = "New mining outside Madre de Dios, ha. 2019 to 2024 confirmed; 2025 = sum of four provisional quarters; 2026 = three provisional quarters. Departments with at least 100 ha in total.")
write_csv(bind_rows(k5_dep, k5_tot), file.path(OUT, "table5_kpi5_outside_mdd.csv"))

k5_q <- out_mdd %>% filter(grepl("Q", period)) %>% group_by(period) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha))
k5_25 <- sum(k5_q$ha[k5_q$period %in% q_last]); k5_26 <- sum(k5_q$ha[k5_q$period %in% q_now])
k5_change <- 100 * (k5_26 / k5_25 - 1)

# Who holds the land: mining title and the El Sira buffer zone (Huánuco)
k5_title <- out_mdd %>% filter(when %in% c("2024", "2025")) %>% group_by(when) %>%
  summarise(titled = 100 * sum(ha[conc]) / sum(ha), sira = 100 * sum(ha[za_sira]) / sum(ha),
            huanuco = 100 * sum(ha[department == "Huánuco"]) / sum(ha), ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(k5_title %>% transmute(Year = when, `New mining outside Madre de Dios (ha)` = fmt(ha),
                                    `in Huánuco (%)` = round(huanuco), `in the El Sira buffer zone (%)` = round(sira),
                                    `inside a mining concession (%)` = round(titled)),
             caption = "Where the new mining outside Madre de Dios is")
k5v <- function(w, d = "Total outside Madre de Dios") bind_rows(k5_dep, k5_tot)$ha[bind_rows(k5_dep, k5_tot)$when == w & bind_rows(k5_dep, k5_tot)$department == d]
log_number("k5_2019", "New mining outside Madre de Dios, 2019", k5v("2019"), "ha", "AMW scar map + GADM")
log_number("k5_2024", "New mining outside Madre de Dios, 2024", k5v("2024"), "ha", "AMW scar map + GADM")
log_number("k5_2025", "New mining outside Madre de Dios, 2025 (4 provisional quarters)", k5v("2025"), "ha", "AMW scar map + GADM")
log_number("k5_huanuco_2019", "New mining in Huánuco, 2019", k5v("2019", "Huánuco"), "ha", "AMW scar map + GADM")
log_number("k5_huanuco_2025", "New mining in Huánuco, 2025 (provisional)", k5v("2025", "Huánuco"), "ha", "AMW scar map + GADM")
log_number("k5_ytd25", "New mining outside Madre de Dios, Q1 to Q3 2025", k5_25, "ha", "AMW scar map + GADM")
log_number("k5_ytd26", "New mining outside Madre de Dios, Q1 to Q3 2026", k5_26, "ha", "AMW scar map + GADM")
log_number("k5_change", "New mining outside Madre de Dios, Q1 to Q3 2026 vs 2025", k5_change, "%", "AMW scar map + GADM")
log_number("k5_titled_2025", "Share of new mining outside Madre de Dios inside a mining concession, 2025", k5_title$titled[k5_title$when == "2025"], "%", "AMW scar map + INGEMMET")
log_number("k5_sira_2025", "Share of new mining outside Madre de Dios in the El Sira buffer zone, 2025", k5_title$sira[k5_title$when == "2025"], "%", "AMW scar map + SERNANP")
```
