**[Description]** Outside Madre de Dios, new mining went from
`r fmt(k5v("2019"))` ha in 2019 to `r fmt(k5v("2024"))` ha in 2024, and
`r fmt(k5v("2025"))` ha in 2025 (provisional). It is still small next to
Madre de Dios, but it is growing. Most of the growth is in **Huánuco**
(`r fmt(k5v("2019", "Huánuco"))` ha in 2019,
`r fmt(k5v("2025", "Huánuco"))` ha in 2025), around the El Sira buffer
zone near Puerto Inca. Pietro found this first. Likitha found a break
out in the El Sira buffer zone with the detections.

**Today KPI 5 is not red:** the first three quarters of 2026 had
`r fmt(k5_26)` ha against `r fmt(k5_25)` ha a year earlier
(`r pct(k5_change)`).

**Be careful with the words.** In 2025,
`r round(k5_title$titled[k5_title$when == "2025"])`% of the new mining
outside Madre de Dios was **inside a mining concession** (titled or in
process). So this is "mining spreading", **not** "illegal mining
spreading". FZS should watch it because a new front can grow fast, and
because the El Sira buffer zone protects a reserve.

**What it does not show.** Same limits as KPI 3. Also, 2025 is the sum
of four provisional quarters, which use a stricter rule than the
confirmed years, so 2025 and 2024 are not exactly comparable. We have
the concession map only for the two map zones on SERNANP's service (UTM
zones 18 and 19), which cover all departments with mining here except
small parts of Amazonas, Cajamarca and Piura.

# How we set the red lines, and would they have warned in time?

**The rules.** We used two kinds of red line. For noisy numbers with a
long history, a statistical rule: "above the recent average plus two
standard deviations". For short or new series, a simple rule that a
director can check by eye: "20% above", "25% more", "more than the worst
year". The table shows each rule and why.

```{r thresholds}
thr <- tribble(
  ~KPI, ~`Red when`, ~`Why this rule`, ~`Today`,
  "1 Gold price in soles", "Ratio to the 3 year average reaches 1.20",
    "A 20% rise in real income is large for a miner; a round number is easy to check",
    paste0(round(latest$ratio, 2), " in ", format(latest$date, "%b %Y"), if (latest$signal) ": RED" else ": not red"),
  "2 Peru's gold gap", paste0("12 month gap more than ", round(X, 1), " points above one year earlier"),
    "The gap is always high, so we watch jumps. X = 2014 to 2016 average change + 2 standard deviations",
    paste0(sprintf("%+.1f", gap_latest$jump), " points in ", format(gap_latest$date, "%b %Y"), if (gap_latest$signal %in% TRUE) ": RED" else ": not red"),
  "3 New mining in FZS landscapes (reserve)", paste0("A quarter above the largest whole year 2019 to 2024 (", fmt(reserve_base_ha), " ha)"),
    "Some mining appears every year, so 'any mining' would always be red",
    paste0(fmt(reserve_q$ha[reserve_q$period == "2026 Q3"]), " ha in 2026 Q3: ", if (reserve_q$red[reserve_q$period == "2026 Q3"]) "RED" else "not red"),
  "3 New mining in FZS landscapes (buffer zones, native communities)", "Quarters so far this year 25% above the same quarters last year",
    "Same quarters because of the dry season and clouds; 25% is a clear rise, not noise",
    paste0("Tambopata buffer ", pct(yv("Tambopata buffer zone", "change")), ", Amarakaeri ", pct(yv("Amarakaeri buffer zone", "change")),
           ", native communities ", pct(yv("Native communities (all)", "change")), ": RED"),
  "4 Forest that became mining", "Above the previous 5 year average + 2 standard deviations",
    "Standard control chart rule for a long yearly series",
    paste0("2025: reserves and buffer zones RED; all Madre de Dios not red (record year, see KPI 4)"),
  "5 New mining outside Madre de Dios", "Quarters so far this year 25% above the same quarters last year",
    "Same rule as KPI 3 buffer zones",
    paste0(pct(k5_change), ": ", if (k5_change > 25) "RED" else "not red"))
knitr::kable(thr, caption = "The red line of each KPI")
write_csv(thr, file.path(OUT, "table6_red_lines.csv"))
```

**The backtest.** Using only data that were public at the time, when
would each KPI have warned FZS about the 2021 to 2023 surge? We use the
dates when each source was first published. MapBiomas Peru presented
Collection 1 (maps to 2021) on 3 March 2023 (reported by Panamericana
that day), Collection 2 (to 2022) on 15 February 2024 (MapBiomas Peru's
website), Collection 3 (to 2024) on 5 June 2025 (MapBiomas Peru's
website; Mongabay reported it on 12 June), and Collection 4
(to 2025) on 20 August 2026 (Caretas). MAAP published
`r fmt(pub("maap185_2122"))` ha for 2021 and 2022 on 15 June 2023
(#185), and `r fmt(pub("maap208_2123"))` ha for 2021 to 2023 on 8 May
2024 (#208).

```{r backtest}
release <- tribble(~covers_to, ~release_date,
                   2021, as.Date("2023-03-03"), 2022, as.Date("2024-02-15"),
                   2024, as.Date("2025-06-05"), 2025, as.Date("2026-08-20"))   # dates of each collection's presentation
first_release <- function(y) min(release$release_date[release$covers_to >= y])
k1_first <- first_signals$date[first_signals$date >= as.Date("2019-01-01")][1]
k2_first <- episodes$from[episodes$from >= as.Date("2019-01-01")][1]
k4_first <- function(z) { y <- k4$year[k4$zone == z & k4$red %in% TRUE & k4$year %in% 2019:2025]; if (length(y)) y else NA }
delay_months <- sapply(2021:2025, function(y) as.numeric(first_release(y) - as.Date(paste0(y, "-12-31"))) / 30.44)
net_cc <- flows %>% filter(year >= 2005) %>% arrange(year) %>%
  mutate(limit = rollapplyr(lag(net_addition), 5, mean, fill = NA) + 2 * rollapplyr(lag(net_addition), 5, sd, fill = NA),
         red = net_addition > limit)
net_years <- net_cc$year[net_cc$red %in% TRUE & net_cc$year %in% 2019:2024]
mdd_years <- k4_first("All Madre de Dios"); res_years_red <- k4_first("Inside the reserves"); za_years_red <- k4_first("Buffer zones")

bt <- tribble(
  ~KPI, ~`First red (data)`, ~`Public by`, ~Comment,
  "1 Gold price in soles", format(k1_first, "%b %Y"), format(k1_first + 35, "%b %Y"),
     "Before the surge. Red again from late 2024, before the record year 2025",
  "2 Peru's gold gap (jump)", format(k2_first, "%b %Y"), format(k2_first + 61, "%b %Y"),
     "In the first year of the surge; BCRP publishes about two months later. An earlier red period (2017 and 2018) had no surge after it",
  "3 New mining in FZS landscapes (quarterly)", first_reserve_red, "days after the quarter",
     "Quarterly data start in 2025, so this KPI cannot be tested on the surge. The yearly detections did not rise in 2021 to 2023",
  "4 Forest that became mining, all Madre de Dios", paste(mdd_years, collapse = ", "), format(first_release(min(mdd_years)), "%d %b %Y"),
     paste0("Each year was first mapped ", round(min(delay_months)), " to ", round(max(delay_months)), " months after it ended (", paste(round(delay_months), collapse = ", "), " months for 2021 to 2025)"),
  "4 Forest that became mining, reserves / buffer zones", paste0(paste(res_years_red, collapse = ", "), " / ", paste(za_years_red, collapse = ", ")),
     format(first_release(min(c(res_years_red, za_years_red), na.rm = TRUE)), "%d %b %Y"), "Inside the reserves from 2023; buffer zones in 2025",
  "5 New mining outside Madre de Dios", "not red", "days after the quarter", "Quarterly data start in 2025; cannot be tested on the surge",
  "For reference: MAAP mining deforestation", paste0("2021 and 2022: ", fmt(pub("maap185_2122")), " ha"), "15 Jun 2023",
     "No single year 2023 figure published; we do not subtract totals from different reports",
  "For reference: net addition (same rule as KPI 4)", paste(net_years, collapse = ", "), format(first_release(min(net_years)), "%d %b %Y"), "Pushed up in 2023 by water relabelled as mining")
knitr::kable(bt, caption = "Backtest: when each KPI would first have turned red, and when the data were public")
write_csv(bt, file.path(OUT, "table7_backtest.csv"))
```

```{r revisions, include = FALSE}
c4_peru_2022 <- cov_pol %>% filter(class == MINING, year == 2022) %>% pull(ha) %>% sum()
c4_mdd_2022  <- mdd_level$mining_ha[mdd_level$year == 2022]
log_number("c4_peru_2022", "Mining area, Peru, 2022, as revised in Collection 4", c4_peru_2022, "ha", "MapBiomas C4")
log_number("c4_mdd_2022", "Mining area, Madre de Dios, 2022, as revised in Collection 4", c4_mdd_2022, "ha", "MapBiomas C4")
log_number("rev_mdd_2022", "Revision of Madre de Dios 2022 mining area, Collection 4 vs Collection 2", 100 * (c4_mdd_2022 / pub("c2_mdd_2022") - 1), "%", "MapBiomas C4 vs C2 (typed)")
```

**[Description]** The two early KPIs moved before the yearly maps. KPI 1
was red from `r format(k1_first, "%B %Y")`, and KPI 2 from
`r format(k2_first, "%B %Y")`. The yearly maps first showed the surge on
3 March 2023.

**Three cautions.**

1. **We chose the rules after seeing the data.** We knew a surge
   happened in 2021 to 2023. So the backtest shows what the rules
   *would* have done; it does not prove they work. The fair test is the
   next two years.
2. **We use today's numbers with yesterday's dates.** We use Collection
   4 values with the release dates of earlier collections, because
   earlier Madre de Dios figures are not in a downloadable table. Each
   collection revises earlier years: for 2022, Collection 2 reported
   about `r fmt(pub("c2_mdd_2022"))` ha of mining in Madre de Dios, and
   Collection 4 now reports `r fmt(c4_mdd_2022)` ha
   (`r sprintf("%+.0f", 100*(c4_mdd_2022/pub("c2_mdd_2022")-1))`%). So
   the backtest shows timing, not the exact values FZS would have seen.
3. **The early KPIs also give warnings with no surge after them**
   (KPI 2 in 2017 and 2018). An early signal means "get ready", not
   "mining will rise".

lims <- as.Date(c("2016-01-01", "2026-12-31"))

p1 <- ggplot(filter(gold, date >= lims[1]), aes(date, ratio)) + surge +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.2, colour = col_alert, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(colour = col_main, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "A  KPI 1, early (monthly): gold price in soles / its 3 year average. Red line: 1.20", x = NULL, y = "Ratio")
p2 <- ggplot(filter(bm_roll, date >= lims[1]), aes(date, jump)) + surge +
  geom_hline(yintercept = X, colour = col_alert, linetype = "dashed") + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_grey) +
  geom_line(colour = col_main, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = paste0("B  KPI 2, early (monthly): jump in Peru's gold gap, points. Red line: ", round(X, 1)), x = NULL, y = "points")
delay <- k4 %>% filter(zone == "All Madre de Dios", year >= 2016) %>%
  mutate(end = as.Date(paste0(year, "-12-31")), public = sapply(year, first_release) %>% as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01"))
p3 <- ggplot(delay) + surge +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = as.Date(paste0(year, "-01-15")), xmax = as.Date(paste0(year, "-12-15")), ymin = 0, ymax = ha, fill = red %in% TRUE)) +
  geom_segment(data = filter(delay, year >= 2020), aes(x = end, xend = public, y = ha, yend = ha), colour = "grey35", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(data = filter(delay, year >= 2020), aes(public, ha), shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = col_main, `TRUE` = col_alert), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +

q_plot <- k3 %>% filter(quarterly, landscape %in% watch[1:3]) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(sprintf("%s-%02d-15", substr(period, 1, 4), 3 * as.integer(substr(period, 7, 7)) - 1)),
         landscape = droplevels(landscape))
p4 <- ggplot(q_plot, aes(date, ha, fill = landscape)) +
  geom_col(width = 80) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Tambopata (inside reserve)" = col_alert, "Tambopata buffer zone" = col_soft, "Amarakaeri buffer zone" = col_grey)) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2024-09-01"), y = max(q_plot$ha) * 0.6, label = "quarterly data\nstart in 2025", hjust = 1, size = 3, colour = "grey40") +
  labs(title = "D  KPI 3, now (quarterly, provisional): new mining in FZS landscapes, ha", x = NULL, y = "ha", fill = NULL)
(p1 / p2 / p3 / p4) + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 1.3, 1)) &
  scale_x_date(limits = lims, date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y", expand = c(0.01, 0)) &
  plot_annotation(title = "Early signals moved in 2020 and 2021; the yearly maps showed the surge only in March 2023",
                  caption = "Shaded: 2021 to 2023 surge. Sources: World Bank Pink Sheet (Oct 2026); BCRP; MapBiomas Peru Collection 4; Amazon Mining Watch (3 Oct 2026); SERNANP.",
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12.5)))
ggsave(file.path(OUT, "fig_main.png"), width = 9.5, height = 10, dpi = 250, bg = "white")

# Context: other signals we checked

These signals are useful to understand the problem, and some are strong
for one country. But each has a problem that stops it from being one of
FZS's five yearly indicators. They are descriptions only; none of them
shows what causes mining.

```{r regional-read}
num <- function(x) as.numeric(gsub(",", "", x))
ctry <- c(`604` = "Peru", `170` = "Colombia", `76` = "Brazil", `68` = "Bolivia", `218` = "Ecuador",
          `862` = "Venezuela", `328` = "Guyana", `740` = "Suriname", `484` = "Mexico")
read_comtrade <- function(pattern) map_dfr(list.files(REG, pattern, full.names = TRUE), function(f) {
  d <- fromJSON(f)$data
  if (length(d) == 0 || NROW(d) == 0) return(NULL)
  as_tibble(d) %>% filter(customsCode == "C00", motCode == 0, partner2Code == 0, partnerCode == 0) %>%   # drop duplicate rows
    transmute(year = as.integer(period), country = ctry[as.character(reporterCode)], flow = flowCode,
              kg = netWgt, usd = primaryValue, qty = qty)
})
ct_gold <- read_comtrade("^comtrade_gold_exports_")
ct_hg   <- read_comtrade("^comtrade_mercury_")
ct_exc  <- read_comtrade("^comtrade_excavators_")
check("UN Comtrade: Bolivia mercury imports 2016 (kg)", sum(ct_hg$kg[ct_hg$country == "Bolivia" & ct_hg$year == 2016 & ct_hg$flow == "M"]), 224195)
check("UN Comtrade: Peru mercury imports 2014 (kg)", sum(ct_hg$kg[ct_hg$country == "Peru" & ct_hg$year == 2014 & ct_hg$flow == "M"]), 102344)
```

| Signal | What it shows | Why it is context, not a KPI |
|--------|---------------|------------------------------|
| New mining by country (Amazon Mining Watch) | Peru, Colombia, Brazil on one scale | Misses river mining, which is most of Colombia's |
| Gold trade in Colombia and Brazil | Where illegal gold enters the legal chain | No export gap to measure; smuggling moves outside the data |
| Mercury imports | Legal mercury collapsed; supply moved to Bolivia and smuggling | Legal trade no longer measures mercury use |
| Coca | Shares land with gold mining | Moves with eradication; prices stop in 2023; no tested link to gold |
| Malaria in Brazilian garimpos | People working in mining, also on rivers | Strong for Brazil only; depends on testing |
| Aviation fuel in Brazil | Supply of remote garimpos by plane | Legal uses too; series ends in 2024 |
| Dredges seized in Colombia | River mining machines | Measures police effort as much as mining |
| Dredges in Loreto (MAAP) | River mining in Peru | Irregular reports; no count for Madre de Dios rivers |
| Excavator imports | Machines for mining | Also used for roads and farms |
| Traffic at highway tolls (Likitha) | Trucks and people moving on the mining road | Only 3 tolls; one toll did not count for 16 months; we do not know what trucks carry |

## New mining by country

```{r regional-amw}
read_gadm0 <- function(cc) st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", normalizePath(file.path(REG, sprintf("gadm41_%s_0.json.zip", cc))), "/", sprintf("gadm41_%s_0.json", cc)), quiet = TRUE)
countries <- bind_rows(dep1 %>% st_union() %>% st_sf(geometry = .) %>% mutate(country = "Peru"),
                       read_gadm0("COL") %>% transmute(country = "Colombia"), read_gadm0("BRA") %>% transmute(country = "Brazil"))
amw_c <- amw_pts_all %>% mutate(country = countries$country[sapply(st_intersects(amw_pts_all, countries), function(i) if (length(i)) i[1] else NA)],
                                country = replace_na(country, "Other Amazon countries"),
                                period = if_else(grepl("^Q", onset), paste0("20", substr(onset, 3, 4), " Q", substr(onset, 2, 2)), onset)) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()
amw_country <- amw_c %>% filter(period != "2018") %>% count(country, period) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = country, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>% arrange(period)
knitr::kable(amw_country, caption = "Amazon Mining Watch: new mining patches by country and first period (2019 to 2024 confirmed; quarters provisional)")
write_csv(amw_country, file.path(OUT, "tableR1_amw_by_country.csv"))
yq <- function(cn, yy) sum(amw_c$country == cn & amw_c$period %in% paste(yy, c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3")))
amw_yoy <- tibble(country = c("Peru", "Colombia", "Brazil", "Other Amazon countries")) %>%
  mutate(q2025 = map_int(country, yq, yy = 2025), q2026 = map_int(country, yq, yy = 2026), change_pct = 100 * (q2026 / q2025 - 1))
knitr::kable(amw_yoy %>% mutate(change_pct = round(change_pct)), caption = "New patches in Q1 to Q3 2026 against Q1 to Q3 2025, by country")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(amw_yoy))) log_number(paste0("amw_chg_", gsub(" ", "_", tolower(amw_yoy$country[i]))), paste("AMW new patches Q1 to Q3 2026 vs 2025,", amw_yoy$country[i]), amw_yoy$change_pct[i], "%", "Amazon Mining Watch + GADM")
ma <- read_csv(file.path(REG, "coursepack_mining_area.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
check("Course pack: Brazil artisanal mining in all indigenous lands, 2025 (ha)", ma$mining_artisanal_ha[ma$territory == "all indigenous lands combined" & ma$year == 2025], 39915)
```

**[Description]** Amazon Mining Watch sees new mining in all three
countries, but very little in Colombia, because most Colombian Amazon
mining is on rivers. Colombia's official yearly measure is the
UNODC and Ministry of Mines survey: `r fmt(pub("evoa_2025"))` ha of
alluvial gold mining on land in 2025, `r pub("evoa_illicit")`% of it
illicit, with river mining alerts in `r pub("evoa_river_sectors")`
sectors of 11 Amazon rivers. It is published only as press releases
and PDFs. For Brazil, MapBiomas (course pack) records
`r fmt(ma$mining_artisanal_ha[ma$territory == "all indigenous lands combined" & ma$year == 2025])`
ha of artisanal mining inside indigenous lands in 2025.

## Gold trade in Colombia and Brazil

```{r col-bra-gold}
anm <- read_csv(file.path(REG, "colombia_anm_gold_production.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>%
  mutate(kg = num(volumenes_de_explotacion) / 1000, year = as.integer(a_o_liquidado))
col_prod <- anm %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(prod_t = sum(kg, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000)
check("ANM Colombia: declared gold production 2023 (t)", col_prod$prod_t[col_prod$year == 2023], 61.34, tol = 0.01)
exports_value <- ct_gold %>% group_by(year, country) %>% summarise(usd_bn = sum(usd) / 1e9, .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(exports_value %>% filter(country %in% c("Peru", "Colombia", "Brazil", "Bolivia", "Ecuador", "Guyana", "Suriname"), year >= 2016) %>%
               mutate(usd_bn = round(usd_bn, 2)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = country, values_from = usd_bn),
             caption = "Gold exports (HS 7108), USD billion, as reported to UN Comtrade (blank = not yet reported)")
write_csv(exports_value, file.path(OUT, "tableR3_gold_exports_comtrade.csv"))
log_number("co_prod_2024", "Colombia declared gold production, 2024", col_prod$prod_t[col_prod$year == 2024], "t", "ANM r85m-vv6c")
log_number("co_prod_2025", "Colombia declared gold production, 2025", col_prod$prod_t[col_prod$year == 2025], "t", "ANM r85m-vv6c")
log_number("br_exp_2025", "Brazil gold exports, 2025", exports_value$usd_bn[exports_value$country == "Brazil" & exports_value$year == 2025], "USD bn", "UN Comtrade HS 7108")

sw <- read_delim(file.path(REG, "swiss_gold_imports_by_origin.csv"), delim = ";", show_col_types = FALSE)
swiss <- sw %>% filter(Control_code == 911, Country_txt %in% c("Peru", "Colombia", "Brazil", "Bolivia", "Ecuador", "Suriname")) %>%
  group_by(Country_txt, year) %>% summarise(t = sum(Quantity_kg) / 1000, .groups = "drop")
check("Swiss customs: mined gold imported from Peru, 2025 (kg)", 1000 * swiss$t[swiss$Country_txt == "Peru" & swiss$year == 2025], 140922)
knitr::kable(swiss %>% mutate(t = round(t, 1)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = t),
             caption = paste0("Switzerland's imports of mined gold (control code 911) by origin, tonnes gross weight (", max(sw$year), " = January to ", month.name[max(sw$month[sw$year == max(sw$year)])], ")"))
```

**[Description]** In **Colombia**, the value of gold exports is about
equal to or below the value of declared production, so there is no
export gap to measure. Illegal gold probably enters the legal chain
*before* export, declared as production **[Interpretation, not
tested]**. Declared production was
`r fmt(col_prod$prod_t[col_prod$year == 2024], 1)` t in 2024 and
`r fmt(col_prod$prod_t[col_prod$year == 2025], 1)` t in 2025. In
**Brazil**, gold registered by garimpos fell from
`r fmt(pub("escolhas_garimpo_2022"))` kg in 2022 to
`r fmt(pub("escolhas_garimpo_2025"))` kg in 2025 (Instituto Escolhas,
from royalty data), after new rules in 2023, while exports reached
USD `r round(exports_value$usd_bn[exports_value$country == "Brazil" & exports_value$year == 2025], 1)`
bn in 2025. Less declared garimpo gold does not mean less garimpo:
Escolhas argues that the gold now leaves by smuggling.

## Mercury

```{r mercury}
# 2025 is left out: several countries had not reported a full year when we downloaded (e.g. Bolivia shows 0 kg)
hg_m <- ct_hg %>% filter(flow == "M", year <= 2024, country %in% c("Peru", "Colombia", "Brazil", "Bolivia", "Guyana")) %>%
  group_by(year, country) %>% summarise(t = sum(kg, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000, .groups = "drop")
hg_mx <- ct_hg %>% filter(flow == "X", country == "Mexico") %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(t = sum(kg, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000)
knitr::kable(hg_m %>% mutate(t = round(t, 1)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = country, values_from = t) %>%
               left_join(hg_mx %>% transmute(year, `Mexico exports` = round(t, 1)), "year") %>% arrange(year),
             caption = "Mercury (HS 280540): imports by country and Mexico's exports, tonnes, 2010 to 2024 (blank = no row reported)")
write_csv(hg_m, file.path(OUT, "tableR4_mercury_imports.csv"))
```

```{r fig-mercury, fig.height = 3.6}
ggplot(hg_m, aes(year, t, colour = country)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Peru = col_alert, Colombia = col_soft, Brazil = "#27AE60", Bolivia = col_main, Guyana = col_grey), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2024, 2)) +
  labs(title = "Legal mercury imports: Peru and Colombia collapsed, Bolivia took over",
       x = NULL, y = "tonnes", caption = "Source: UN Comtrade, HS 280540, imports as reported by each country. Missing years are gaps.")
ggsave(file.path(OUT, "figR_mercury.png"), width = 9, height = 3.6, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```

**[Description]** Legal mercury imports into Peru fell from
`r round(hg_m$t[hg_m$country == "Peru" & hg_m$year == 2011])` t (2011)
to almost nothing after 2015. Colombia's fell from
`r round(hg_m$t[hg_m$country == "Colombia" & hg_m$year == 2016])` t
(2016) to about 2 t a year, once its ban on mercury in mining took
effect (Ley 1658 of 2013, in force for mining from 2018). In the same
years Bolivia became the largest importer in the region
(`r round(hg_m$t[hg_m$country == "Bolivia" & hg_m$year == 2016])` t in
2016). Mining did not stop, so **legal imports no longer measure mercury
use**. The Environmental Investigation Agency (2025) documented hidden
shipments from Mexico to Peru and Colombia. What FZS can track instead
is seizures (no open series exists) and mercury in people and fish
(sampling on the ground).

## Coca

```{r coca}
coca <- read_csv(file.path(REG, "colombia_coca_hectares_municipality.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("_"), names_to = "year", values_to = "ha") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(sub("_", "", year)), ha = replace_na(as.numeric(ha), 0))
check("Colombia coca cultivation, national total 2024 (ha)", sum(coca$ha[coca$year == 2024]), 261386)
amazon_deps <- c("PUTUMAYO", "CAQUETÁ", "GUAVIARE", "AMAZONAS", "GUAINÍA", "VAUPÉS")
coca_amz <- coca %>% filter(departamento %in% amazon_deps, year >= 2015) %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha))
cp <- read_excel(file.path(REG, "peru_devida_coca_leaf_prices_2020_2023.xlsx"))
mes <- c(Enero = 1, Febrero = 2, Marzo = 3, Abril = 4, Mayo = 5, Junio = 6, Julio = 7, Agosto = 8, Setiembre = 9, Octubre = 10, Noviembre = 11, Diciembre = 12)
coca_p <- cp %>% pivot_longer(-ZEI, names_to = "m", values_to = "pen_kg") %>%
  mutate(month = mes[str_extract(m, "^[A-Za-z]+")], year = as.integer(str_extract(m, "\\d{4}")), date = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", year, month))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(pen_kg))
knitr::kable(coca_p %>% filter(ZEI %in% c("Sur Amazónico", "Triple Frontera", "NACIONAL"), month %in% c(1, 7)) %>%
               transmute(Zone = ZEI, Month = format(date, "%b %Y"), `Leaf price (soles per kg)` = round(pen_kg, 2)) %>%
               pivot_wider(names_from = Month, values_from = `Leaf price (soles per kg)`),
             caption = "Peru: coca leaf price by zone (DEVIDA), soles per kg, January and July of each year")
log_number("co_coca_amz_2024", "Coca cultivation in Colombia's six Amazon departments, 2024", coca_amz$ha[coca_amz$year == 2024], "ha", "MinJusticia/SIMCI acs4-3wgp")
```

**[Description]** Coca and gold mining share land: according to UNODC
and Colombia's Ministry of Mines, `r pub("evoa_coca_overlap")`% of the
land with alluvial gold mining in 2025 overlapped with coca. In
Colombia's six Amazon departments coca covered
`r fmt(coca_amz$ha[coca_amz$year == 2024])` ha in 2024. In Peru, the
national coca leaf price fell from
S/ `r round(coca_p$pen_kg[coca_p$ZEI == "NACIONAL" & coca_p$date == as.Date("2020-01-01")], 2)`
per kg (January 2020) to
S/ `r round(min(coca_p$pen_kg[coca_p$ZEI == "NACIONAL"]), 2)` (its
lowest) and later recovered. The idea that people switch to gold when
coca prices fall is possible but **not tested** in the evidence we
found, and coca also moves with forced eradication.

## Signals of activity: malaria, fuel, dredges, machines

```{r malaria}
mal <- map_dfr(list.files(REG, "^brazil_malaria_special_areas_\\d{4}\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE),
               ~ read_csv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c")))
names(mal) <- c("cod_mun", "mun", "uf", "year", "area", "n")
mal <- mal %>% filter(year != "All", area != "All", uf != "All") %>% mutate(n = num(n), year = as.integer(year))   # drop subtotal rows
mal_y <- mal %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(total = sum(n), garimpo = sum(n[area == "Garimpo"]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(share = 100 * garimpo / total)
check("Brazil Ministry of Health: autochthonous malaria cases 2022", mal_y$total[mal_y$year == 2022], 128968)
mal_uf <- mal %>% filter(area == "Garimpo") %>% group_by(uf, year) %>% summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(mal_y %>% transmute(Year = year, `All cases` = fmt(total), `Caught in garimpo areas` = fmt(garimpo), `Share (%)` = round(share, 1)),
             caption = "Brazil: malaria cases caught in Brazil, and those caught in a garimpo area (2026: January to early October)")
write_csv(mal_uf, file.path(OUT, "tableR5_brazil_malaria_garimpo_by_state.csv"))
mv <- function(y) mal_y$garimpo[mal_y$year == y]
log_number("br_mal_garimpo_2022", "Brazil malaria cases caught in garimpo areas, 2022", mv(2022), "cases", "Ministério da Saúde, Tableau 'Dados para Cidadão'")
log_number("br_mal_garimpo_2025", "Brazil malaria cases caught in garimpo areas, 2025", mv(2025), "cases", "Ministério da Saúde")
log_number("br_mal_garimpo_2026", "Brazil malaria cases caught in garimpo areas, 2026 to early October", mv(2026), "cases", "Ministério da Saúde")
```

```{r fig-malaria, fig.height = 3.8}
mal_uf %>% filter(uf %in% c("PA", "RR", "AP", "MT", "AM")) %>%
  mutate(uf = recode(uf, PA = "Pará", RR = "Roraima (Yanomami)", AP = "Amapá", MT = "Mato Grosso", AM = "Amazonas")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, n, fill = uf)) + geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Pará" = col_main, "Roraima (Yanomami)" = col_alert, "Amapá" = col_soft, "Mato Grosso" = col_grey, "Amazonas" = "#5DADE2"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2018:2026) +
  labs(title = "Brazil: malaria cases caught in garimpo areas, by state", subtitle = "2026: January to early October only",
       x = NULL, y = "cases", caption = "Source: Ministério da Saúde, SIVEP Malária, 'Dados para Cidadão' dashboard (área especial = Garimpo).")
ggsave(file.path(OUT, "figR_brazil_malaria.png"), width = 9, height = 3.8, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```

**[Description]** In Brazil, malaria caught in garimpo areas rose from
`r fmt(mv(2018))` cases (2018) to `r fmt(mv(2022))` (2022), fell to
`r fmt(mv(2025))` in 2025, and reached `r fmt(mv(2026))` by early
October 2026, already `r round(100 * mv(2026) / mv(2025))`% of the 2025
total. In Roraima (Yanomami land) cases fell sharply after the federal
operation of 2023; in Pará (Munduruku land and the Tapajós) they stayed
high. Malaria follows people who work in garimpos, so it measures
**activity**, and it also sees mining on rivers. It depends on how much
testing is done, and garimpos inside indigenous lands may be recorded as
"indigenous area".

```{r fuel}
read_anp <- function(f) { d <- read_delim(file.path(REG, f), delim = ";", show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
  names(d) <- c("year", "region", "uf", "product", "ibge", "mun", "sales"); d %>% mutate(year = as.integer(year), sales = num(sales)) }
avgas <- read_anp("brazil_anp_avgas_municipality.csv"); diesel <- read_anp("brazil_anp_diesel_municipality.csv")
hubs <- c(`1400100` = "Boa Vista (RR)", `1503606` = "Itaituba (PA)", `1400050` = "Alto Alegre (RR)", `1503804` = "Jacareacanga (PA)")
fuel <- bind_rows(avgas %>% mutate(fuel = "Aviation gasoline"), diesel %>% mutate(fuel = "Diesel")) %>%
  filter(ibge %in% names(hubs), year >= 2014) %>% mutate(place = hubs[ibge]) %>% group_by(fuel, place, year) %>% summarise(m3 = sum(sales) / 1000, .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(fuel %>% filter(fuel == "Aviation gasoline", place %in% c("Boa Vista (RR)", "Itaituba (PA)")) %>% mutate(m3 = round(m3)) %>%
               pivot_wider(names_from = place, values_from = m3) %>% select(-fuel),
             caption = "Brazil: aviation gasoline sales, thousand litres (ANP)")
av_bv <- function(y) avgas$sales[avgas$ibge == "1400100" & avgas$year == y]
check("ANP: aviation gasoline sales, Boa Vista, 2021 (litres)", av_bv(2021), 3207403)
log_number("br_avgas_bv_2021", "Aviation gasoline sales, Boa Vista, 2021", av_bv(2021), "litres", "ANP")
log_number("br_avgas_bv_2024", "Aviation gasoline sales, Boa Vista, 2024", av_bv(2024), "litres", "ANP")
write_csv(fuel, file.path(OUT, "tableR6_brazil_fuel_hubs.csv"))
```

**[Description]** Small planes supply garimpos on Yanomami land from
Boa Vista. Aviation gasoline sales there rose from
`r fmt(av_bv(2016) / 1000)` thousand litres (2016) to
`r fmt(av_bv(2021) / 1000)` (2021) and fell to
`r fmt(av_bv(2024) / 1000)` (2024), after the federal operation that
started in 2023. Aviation fuel also has legal uses, and the series ends
in 2024.

```{r dredges}
md <- read_csv(file.path(REG, "colombia_mindefensa_machinery_seized.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(substr(fecha_hecho, 1, 4)), dredge = grepl("DRAGA", clase_de_bien))

  group_by(region, year) %>% summarise(n = sum(cantidad), .groups = "drop")
check("MinDefensa: dredges destroyed or seized in Amazonas department, 2025", sum(dredges_col$n[dredges_col$region == "Amazonas" & dredges_col$year == 2025]), 56)
knitr::kable(dredges_col %>% pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n, values_fill = 0),
             caption = paste0("Colombia: dredges seized or destroyed, by department (", max(md$year), ": to ", format(max(as.Date(substr(md$fecha_hecho, 1, 10))), "%B"), ")"))
write_csv(dredges_col, file.path(OUT, "tableR7_colombia_dredges.csv"))
co_dr_amz_2025 <- sum(dredges_col$n[dredges_col$region != "Rest of Colombia" & dredges_col$year == 2025])
log_number("co_dredges_amazon_2025", "Dredges seized or destroyed in Colombia's six Amazon departments, 2025", co_dr_amz_2025, "dredges", "MinDefensa dxs6-mdeg")

dredges_pe <- tribble(
  ~Published, ~Source, ~Area, ~Period, ~Figure,
  "29 Sep 2025", "MAAP #233", "Loreto", "2017 to 2025", paste(fmt(pub("maap233_loreto")), "dredges recorded"),
  "29 Sep 2025", "MAAP #233", "Nanay river (Loreto)", "2017 to 2025", paste0(fmt(pub("maap233_nanay")), " recorded, of which ", pub("maap233_nanay25"), " in 2025"),
  "29 Sep 2025", "MAAP #233", "Peruvian Amazon", "to 2025", paste("mining in", pub("maap233_water"), "water bodies"),
  "17 Aug 2026", "MAAP (via Actualidad Ambiental)", "Loreto", "2025 to Jun 2026", paste0("more than ", pub("aa_records"), " records, ", pub("aa_rivers"), " rivers"))

write_csv(dredges_pe, file.path(OUT, "tableR10_peru_dredges_published.csv"))
```

**[Description]** In Colombia, the security forces seized or destroyed
`r co_dr_amz_2025` dredges in the six Amazon departments in 2025. These
counts measure **police effort** as much as mining: more dredges
destroyed can mean more mining or more operations. In Peru, the only
repeated public count of dredges is MAAP's, mostly for Loreto, read by
hand from images; records are not unique dredges (the same dredge is
seen many times). No source counts dredges on Madre de Dios rivers.

```{r excavators}
exc <- ct_exc %>% group_by(year, country) %>% summarise(units = sum(qty, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(exc %>% mutate(units = round(units)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = country, values_from = units),
             caption = "Imports of excavators (HS 842952), units, UN Comtrade (blank = not yet reported)")
write_csv(exc, file.path(OUT, "tableR8_excavator_imports.csv"))
```

**[Description]** Between 2019 and 2024 excavator imports grew
`r round(exc$units[exc$country == "Peru" & exc$year == 2024] / exc$units[exc$country == "Peru" & exc$year == 2019], 1)` times
in Peru,
`r round(exc$units[exc$country == "Colombia" & exc$year == 2024] / exc$units[exc$country == "Colombia" & exc$year == 2019], 1)` times
in Colombia and
`r round(exc$units[exc$country == "Brazil" & exc$year == 2024] / exc$units[exc$country == "Brazil" & exc$year == 2019], 1)` times
in Brazil. Excavators are also used for roads, farms and legal mining,
so this is weak as a mining measure on its own.

**Traffic at highway tolls.** Likitha studied traffic at the three toll
stations on the Interoceanic Highway (OSITRAN data, separate file).
Traffic grew much more at the toll next to the mining area than at the
two other tolls. It is a good sign of activity on the mining road, but
there are only three tolls, one toll stopped counting vehicles for 16
months after the 2023 protests, and we do not know what the trucks
carry. So it is context, not a KPI.

# Did the satellite methods change?

Our indicators compare years, so a change in *how* images are classified
can look like a change in mining. We checked the documents of each
satellite source.

- **MapBiomas Peru (Collection 4).** Every collection classifies all
  years again from 1985, so values change between collections (Madre de
  Dios, 2022: about `r fmt(pub("c2_mdd_2022"))` ha in Collection 2,
  `r fmt(c4_mdd_2022)` ha in Collection 4). The images come from
  several Landsat satellites over time. The Collection 4 method
  documents were offline when we checked (14 October 2026). The method
  is described as following MapBiomas Brazil's mining method, which
  corrects each year using the year before and the year after. The last
  year (here 2025) has no "year after", so it is the least corrected and
  the most likely to change in the next collection.
- **Amazon Mining Watch.** Its README (3 October 2026) says the model
  "was wholly redeveloped in 2026 and the data recomputed starting from
  year 2018". Older MAAP figures based on Amazon Mining Watch are
  therefore not comparable with today's files. Quarterly detections use
  a stricter rule than yearly ones. The scar map is "in development" and
  its areas "run large".
- **MapBiomas Brazil (course pack).** The municipality table is
  Collection 10.1 and `mining_area.csv` is Collection 11; we do not
  combine them.
- **MAAP.** Its long series joins different methods over time, and its
  2021 to 2023 total was revised from `r fmt(pub("maap195_2123"))` ha
  (#195) to `r fmt(pub("maap208_2123"))` ha (#208).

**A possible break in 2023.** The flows between water and mining change
suddenly in 2023, and not only in Madre de Dios:

```{r method-break}
flip_tab <- tr_pol %>% filter(year >= 2016) %>%
  mutate(region = if_else(unit == "Madre de Dios", "Madre de Dios", "Rest of Peru"),
         flow = case_when(class_from %in% WATER & class_to == MINING ~ "Water to mining",
                          class_from == MINING & class_to %in% WATER ~ "Mining to water")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(flow)) %>% group_by(region, flow, year) %>% summarise(ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(flip_tab %>% mutate(ha = fmt(ha)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = ha) %>% arrange(flow, region),
             caption = "Flows between water and mining (ha per year), MapBiomas Peru Collection 4")
write_csv(flip_tab, file.path(OUT, "table1c_water_mining_flips.csv"))
fv <- function(r, fl, y) flip_tab$ha[flip_tab$region == r & flip_tab$flow == fl & flip_tab$year %in% y]
log_number("w2m_rest_2023", "Water to mining, rest of Peru, 2023", fv("Rest of Peru", "Water to mining", 2023), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
log_number("m2w_mdd_2023", "Mining to water, Madre de Dios, 2023", fv("Madre de Dios", "Mining to water", 2023), "ha", "MapBiomas C4 transitions")
```

**[Description]** In Madre de Dios, on average
`r fmt(mean(fv("Madre de Dios", "Mining to water", 2019:2022)))` ha of
mining land a year was relabelled as water in 2019 to 2022, but only
`r fmt(fv("Madre de Dios", "Mining to water", 2023))` ha in 2023. At the
same time `r fmt(fv("Madre de Dios", "Water to mining", 2023))` ha of
water was relabelled as mining. In the rest of Peru, water to mining
also jumped, from an average of
`r fmt(mean(fv("Rest of Peru", "Water to mining", 2016:2022)))` ha a year
in 2016 to 2022 to `r fmt(fv("Rest of Peru", "Water to mining", 2023))`
ha in 2023. Miners going back to old pits in Madre de Dios would not
explain the same jump in the rest of Peru, so part of the 2023 change
may come from how this collection classified ponds and mining
**[Interpretation, not tested]**. We could not confirm this in the
documents. KPI 4 does not use these flows, which is one more reason to
prefer forest that became mining.

# What the data cannot see

- **Rivers and mercury.** No land map measures dredges, or mercury in
  water, fish and people. Dredge counts exist only for Loreto (Peru) and
  as police seizures (Colombia). Mercury needs sampling on the ground.
- **Legality.** "Mining" includes legal mining in the mining corridor.
  A mining title does not prove legality, and no title does not prove
  illegality. Only mining inside a reserve is clearly illegal.
- **Revisions and model changes.** Every MapBiomas collection revises
  earlier years, and Amazon Mining Watch rebuilt its model in 2026 and
  replaces its files. FZS should save each version it uses and write
  the version next to every number.
- **Targets.** If an indicator becomes a target (for example, mining
  inside a reserve), miners and agencies may respond to the number
  rather than to the problem.

```{r save-numbers}
numbers <- bind_rows(numbers, published %>% mutate(source = paste(source, "(typed by hand)"))) %>% mutate(value = round(value, 2))
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(numbers$id)))
write_csv(numbers, file.path(OUT, "numbers_in_brief.csv"))
knitr::kable(numbers, caption = "Numbers produced or quoted in this notebook (output/numbers_in_brief.csv)")
sessionInfo()
```
